acanthostega.name: ACANTHOSTEGA
facts: Acanthostega is one of the first vertebrate animals to have recognizable limbs. That means it is a crucial step in the development of aquatic creatures into terrestrial animals!
This roughly two-foot long creature lived 360 million years ago. That means it's roughly 276 million years older than the T. rex!
Acanthostega spends most of its time in the water, but hunts by snapping at prey on the water's edge! This behavior develops into full-blown terrestrial hunting in its descendants.
Acanthostega is a shallow-water dweller and an evolutionary link between fish and true amphibians. This suggests that animals specialized for shallow waters are the ancestors of amphibians.

acrocanthosaurus.name: ACROCANTHOSAURUS
facts: Acrocanthosaurus means 'high spined lizard.' This apex predator looks like a Tyrannosaurus with a hunchback!
At 38 feet and weighing over 6 tons, the Acrocanthosaurus was one of the biggest land-dwelling predators ever!
The best preserved Acrocanthosaurus skeleton ever discovered was found in Oklahoma - its name is Fran!
The Acrocanthosaurus has incredibly short forelimbs - so short, it can’t even scratch its own neck!

aerotitan.name: AEROTITAN
facts: Did you know that Aerotitan is Greek for 'air titan'?
Fossils of the Aerotitan were discovered in 2012 in Patagonia, Argentina. They date back to the Late Cretaceous period!
Did you know that the Aerotitan has no teeth? They have an elongated snout and toothless jaws instead!
The Aerotitan has a wingspan of 16 feet. That's larger than a Bede BD-5 small aircraft!

ailurarctos.name: AILURARCTOS
facts: The Ailurarctos is an extinct genus of panda from the Late Miocene of Chine. It existed approximately 8 million years ago, making it one of the oldest known ursids!
Similar to modern giant pandas, the Ailurarctos had what is known as a false thumb. The false thumb is a carpal bone that has been enlarged and can function as an opposable thumb.
The existence of the Ailurarctos' false thumb allowed it to grip bamboo, which suggests that a panda's bamboo diet goes back as far as 6 or 7 million years ago!

The teeth of the Ailurarctos differ from modern pandas, suggesting mosaic evolution occurred during the last 2 million years. Mosaic evolution is the idea that evolutionary change takes place in some body parts without simultaneous changes in other parts.

alangasaurus.name: ALANGASAURUS
facts: Created by InGen for Jurassic World, the Alangasaurus has striped, mottled scales and a distinct nose fin!
Did you know that Alangasaurus means 'phoenix lizard'? This hybrid combines the DNA of an Alanqa and Majungasaurus.
The Alangasaurus is much lighter in build than its Majungasaurus progenitor, weighing in at 900 lbs. That's less than a cow!
What the Alangasaurus loses in sheer brute strength it makes up for in speed and agility, thanks to its light frame.

alanqa.name: ALANQA
facts: Did you know that the Alanqa is named after a mythological Arabian phoenix?
Discovered in Morocco in 2008, Alanqa fossils date back 65 million years to the Late Cretaceous period!
The mythological phoenix, Anqa, was not only huge, but strong enough to carry away an elephant or a whale!
The Alanqa has a wingspan of 13-20 feet. The wandering albatross, by comparison, only has a wingspan of only 12 feet!

albertosaurus.name: ALBERTOSAURUS
facts: Albertosaurus is a Tyrannosauroid, but of a different genus than its better known cousin, Rex.
The Albertosaurus had puny arms. The purpose of these stunted appendages eludes paleontologists.
Albertosaurus derives its name from the site where it was discovered in 1884 - Horseshoe Canyon in Alberta, Canada.
Some scientists have speculated that Albertosaurus' diminished arm size was due to the need to balance the weight from its enormous jaw muscles.

allonogmius.name: ALLONOGMIUS
facts: Like the Allosaurus, Allonogmius is known to prey on large herbivores like Stegosaurus.
Though a land-dwelling creature, Allonogmius's aquatic instincts often lead it to shoreline hunting grounds.
Powerful in shallow water, Allonogmius will sometimes drag prey into shallow pools to gain an environmental advantage.
On land, the large dorsal fin of the Allonogmius helps in heat regulation.

allosaurus.name: ALLOSAURUS
facts: Fossil evidence shows that the Allosaurus and the Stegosaurus often got into scraps!
Did you know that the Allosaurus is the official state fossil of Utah?
In Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's novel, "The Lost World", the Allosaurus was the top predator.
The name Allosaurus is Ancient Greek for 'different lizard'. But one famous skeleton is known by its nickname, 'Big Al'.

amargasaurus.name: AMARGASAURUS
facts: This herbivore can live up to 100 years, if not eaten by a Tyrannosaurus first!
The Amargasaurus ran at speeds up to 31 mph, about as fast as a rhino!
Amargasaurus has large spines on its back that can be used for defense or show!
Like many herbivorous dinosaurs, Amargasaurus travels in herds for protection from predators.

ammonite.name: AMMONITE
facts: Did you know that Ammonite gets its name from the spiral shape of its shell, which resembles tightly coiled rams’ horns?
Ancient Roman author, Pliny the Elder, called Ammonite fossils ‘ammonis cornua’ (‘horns of Ammon’), after the Egyptian god, Ammon.
As excellent swimmers, the Ammonite prefer open water to the sea floor.
The shell of the Ammonites consist of chambers joined together by sutures, which help the Ammonite float.

amphicyon.name: AMPHICYON
facts: Amphicyon is commonly called a 'bear dog' for its mix of the two mammals' body shapes. Its name actually means "ambiguous dog."
Though it has wolf-like teeth and a canine face, this 200 pound, 8 foot omnivore would tower over any living wolf!
There are actually several sub-species of Amphicyon. The largest, Amphicyon ingens, weighed over 1200 pounds!
This large mammal didn't go extinct until the early Pleistocene. That's the beginning of the most recent Ice Age!

amphicyon_gen_2.name: AMPHICYON GEN 2
facts: This InGen creation was possible due to fossils and remains found all over the world!
The found fossils of Amphicyon in different continents tell the tale of its migration across the world, as its population spread.
Despite common traits with today's large cats, its posterior legs are not meant for sprints and quick bursts of speed. Scientists theorize it behaved much more like an ambush predator.
Amphicyon fossils had trouble being correctly identified due to size differences among the samples. It has only recently been corrected after identifying male and female remains.

andrewsarchus.name: ANDREWSARCHUS
facts: The Andrewsarchus gets its name from Roy Chapman Andrews. It means ‘Andrews commander’.
Discovered in 1923, only a skull of the Andrewsarchus was discovered in Inner Mongolia, China.
To recreate the Andrewsarchus for Jurassic World, DNA from the Mesonyx was used, which is believed to be a larger relative.
Did you know that the Andrewsarchus is related to Entelodonts, hippos, and whales?

andrewtherium.name: ANDREWTHERIUM
facts: Andrewtherium is both the longest nosed and largest hippo-like creature the park has ever seen.
Despite the massive canines of the Andrewtherium, which suggest a predatory nature, its diet is almost exclusively shellfish.
Andrewtherium's molars are perfectly designed for crushing shellfish into paste.
Park hands used to feed Andrewtherium shrimp, but after he turned pink, they switched to scallops.

angel.name: ANGEL
facts: This spinoceratops is the sister of another named Rebel.
Despite its name, this dinosaur has a much wilder behavior compared to its brother.
DNA analysis from Angel confirms that the Spinoceratops requires a much colder climate in order to thrive, and experiences considerable discomfort in desert and tropical climates.
Playful behavior observed from Angel and Rebel confirm it is the main way these dinosaurs learn through their continued growth.

animantarx.name: ANIMANTARX
facts: This rare creature is theorized to have lived between 106 and 97 million years ago.
Its discovery is recent, due to a very small quantity of fossils and specimens to study.
The Animantarx was discovered by accident since its still radioactive fossils were detected by scanners during geological studies.

The Animantarx is much smaller than other similar dinosaurs, although almost as well armored. This results in a species with similar defenses but a much smaller food intake required to sustain itself.

ankylodocus.name: ANKYLODOCUS
facts: At 160 feet long, the Ankylodocus is much smaller than its 175 foot long sauropod progenitor!
Did you know that Ankylodocus means 'fused beam' on account of its size and armor?
What makes an Ankylodocus a force to be reckoned with is its 8 foot long clubbed tail. Imagine a dinosaur with a flail!
The Ankyldocus' armor functions like chainmail for this otherwise gentle giant.

ankylosaurus.name: ANKYLOSAURUS
facts: Did you know Ankylosaurus means 'fused' or 'stiffened lizard'? It was one of the last dinosaurs to go extinct.
Known for its armor, the Ankylosaurus has large bone plates embedded into its skin like an armadillo or modern crocodile.
The club-like tail of the Ankylosaurus can land a devastating blow, breaking bones on impact!
The Ankylosaurus has one of the smallest brains to body ratios. Its intelligence is similar to its close cousin, the Stegosaurus!

ankylosaurus_gen_2.name: ANKYLOSAURUS GEN 2
facts: Just like the original Ankylosaurus, this Gen 2 prefers to feed on low-lying ferns and cycads.
This creature existed during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 66 million years ago.
Ankylosaurus Gen 2's intricate nasal passages allow it to perform a variety of honking and snorting sounds.
This creature's well-armored body is designed to fend off Tyrannosaurus rex attacks.

antarctopelta.name: ANTARCTOPELTA
facts: The Antarctopelta gets its name from Antarctica. It is the first dinosaur to be ever found on the continent!
While modern Antarctica is covered in ice and snow, during the Cretaceous period, the Antarctopelta lived in lush forest.
Although Antarctopelta was discovered in 1986, it was not named until 20 years later!
At around 13 feet in length, the Antarctopelta is as long as some American crocodiles!

anurognathus.name: ANUROGNATHUS
facts: The Anurognathus is a diminutive pterosaur, with a wingspan of only about 1.5 feet, making it one of the smallest flying reptiles of the Mesozoic era.
This pterosaur primarily feeds on insects, using its wide, frog-like mouth to catch and consume prey mid-flight, making it a highly effective aerial insectivore.
The Anurognathus is notable for its very short tail, which contrasts with the long tails of many other pterosaurs, contributing to its compact and agile flying abilities.
Evidence suggests that Anurognathus may have been nocturnal, relying on its large eyes to hunt insects during the night, similar to modern-day nightjars or bats.

apatosaurus.name: APATOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that there was a Transformers autobot who could transform into an Apatosaurus?
Apatosaurus means 'deceptive lizard.' In 1877, its tail bones were unlike other fossils discovered at the time.
In 1914, Winsor McCay created one of the first animated films. It had an Apatosaurus called 'Gertie the Dinosaur.'
This glorious gargantuan has a lifespan of 70 years. The average American life expectancy is around 79 years.

aquilops.name: AQUILOPS
facts: The Aquilops is ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period.
It takes its name from the latin word "Aquila", meaning "eagle", as a reference to the shape of its beak.
The snout beak of the Aquilops serves to dig and unearth roots and other food sources an herbivore would enjoy.
Aquilops remains were unearthed with bite marks matching with a velociraptor's jaw profile. This suggests the Aquilops were prey to the Velociraptor at some point in history.

arambourgiania.name: ARAMBOURGIANIA
facts: Arambourgiania was originally named 'Titanopteryx', but it was changed after it was pointed out the genus name was already in use by a fly.
Arambourgiania's wingspan is estimated to have been roughly 13 meters (43 ft).
Arambourgiania's name comes from the man who discovered their first fossil: Camille Arambourg, who thought he had found a wing metacarpal.
Arambourgiania is roughly the size of a giraffe.

archaeophicyon.name: ARCHAEOPHICYON
facts: Some call this fusion of the Amphicyon and the Archaeotherium the 'tusked wolf!'
This dangerous mammalian hybrid can run faster than a modern grizzly!
The tusks and mane of Archaeophicyon grow larger as it matures.
The large ears of the fully mature Archaeophicyon allow it to pick up the footfalls of even the quietest prey.

archaeotherium.name: ARCHAEOTHERIUM
facts: Archaeotherium means 'ancient beast.' It's a good name for this large fanged boar!
While not very smart, the Archaeotherium has a keen sense of smell, like a modern day wild boar.
Like pigs, Archaeotherium eats almost everything. It hunts, scavenges, and digs for roots and tubers!
Fossilized footprints reveal that the Archaeotherium preyed on the Subhyracodon, an extinct form of rhinoceros. What a beast!

archelon.name: ARCHELON
facts: Did you know that Archelon means ‘ruler turtle’? Its closest modern relative is the leatherback sea turtle!
The Archelon is the largest sea turtle known to exist!
An Archelon can grow up to 13 feet in length and 16 feet in width. That’s bigger than an ambulance!
Unlike the modern turtle, the Archelon does not have a solid shell. Instead, a skeletal framework supports a bony carapace!

arctodus.name: ARCTODUS
facts: Arctodus is also known as the short-faced bear.
One of the largest terrestrial mammalian predators ever, the Arctodus stood around 10 feet tall on its hind legs and could weigh over 1900 pounds!
On all fours, the Arctodus is tall enough to look a human in the eye.
Arctodus went extinct around the same time as most prehistoric megafauna. One theory for this extinction is that these large predators were muscled out of evolution by smaller, faster hunters.

argentinosaurus.name: ARGENTINOSAURUS
facts: The Argentinosaurus is one of the largest known dinosaurs to ever walk the Earth!
Did you know that when the Argentinosaurus was discovered, its leg fossil was mistaken for a giant piece of petrified wood?
Enormous as adults, Argentinosaurus' infants are quite small. They grow 25 times their original size by the time they reach maturity!
Due to their incredible size, the Argentinosaurus can only run 5 miles per hour. That's slower than a swimming sea turtle!

armormata.name: ARMORMATA
facts: Although Armormata's tail fin gives it the appearance of being mid-evolution, it is equipped to thrive on land.
Armormata's name references Squamata; the reptile family which Mosasurus comes from.
This hybrid burrows in mud to regulate its body temperature and protect its soft underbelly while resting.
Armormata has a terrible temper. Its highly aggressive nature likely comes from the aquatic carnivore it was fused from.

australotitan.name: AUSTRALOTITAN
facts: Australotitan is a Titanosaur, a clade it shares with Dreadnoughtus, Argentinosaurus and more!
Titanosaurs are among the largest land animals to ever live. Australotitan stood 21 feet tall at the hip!
Australotitan is the largest known Australian dinosaur.
Australotitan's thighbone alone measures 7 feet!

baculites.name: BACULITES
facts: The Baculites’ name, which means ‘walking stick rock’, comes from the straight shape of its shell!
A Baculite can reach 6 feet in length! Like other cephalopods, it has tentacle-like arms, allowing it to feed on zooplankton.
Although researchers speculated that the Baculites lived vertically, Jurassic World’s equivalent lives horizontally!
Did you know that parts of Baculites shell fossils are sometimes referred to as ‘stone buffaloes’ due to their shape?

bageherpeton.name: BAGEHERPETON
facts: The Bageherpeton is an extinct genus of large, long-snouted temnospondyls known as archaegosaurid.
Bageherpeton originated in the Permian geologic period of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
Like other archaegosaurid, the Bageherpeton is a fully aquatic animal.
Found in the Rio do Rasto Formation, the Bageherpeton got its name from the nearby city of Bagé.

bagehesaurus.name: BAGEHESAURUS
facts: The Bagehesaurus has sharper teeth than its ancestors, giving it a bite you don't want to mess with!
Like the Bageherpeton, the Bagehesaurus enjoys an aquatic habitat, though it can also live comfortably on land.
The Bagehesaurus inherited the distinct sail of Edaphosaurus, which helps scare away predators.
The Bagehesaurus uses its powerful legs to easily glide through water, allowing it to sneak attack enemies.

bajadasaurus.name: BAJADASAURUS
facts: Bajadasaurus is a sauropod from the early Cretaceous period.
Bajadasaurus was discovered in modern day Patagonia, Argentina.
Bajadasaurus' trademark feature are its long neural spines, which may have served as passive defense against predators.
Bajadasaurus is a relatively small and short-necked sauropod, reaching roughly the size of modern Asian elephant.

bananogmius.name: BANANOGMIUS
facts: Did you know that the Bananogmius is related to modern-day angelfish?
Like an angelfish, the Bananogmius has a huge dorsal fin!
The Bananogmius has small, comb-like teeth which it uses to filter food, such as brine shrimp, bloodworms, and daphnia!
A full grown Bananogmius can reach 4-6 feet in length. That’s the same as an ocean sunfish!

barracudasaurus.name: BARRACUDASAURUS
facts: Barracudasaurus is a genus of ichthyosaur, gigantic marine reptiles of the Mesozoic.
Barracudasaurus has elongated conical premaxillary teeth, which may have helped it snag its prey.
The name Barracudasaurus was chosen for this creature because of resemblance to the modern Barracuda.
The discovery of Barracudasaurus in China suggests Ichthyosaurs may have initially evolved in Asia.

baryonyx.name: BARYONYX
facts: Baryonyx means 'Heavy Claw.' It got the name from the large claw on each of its forefingers!
Baryonyx is a riverside predator. Its conical teeth are well adapted for catching and holding onto fish.
The Baryonyx is a member of the Spinosaur family, and is related to the Spinosaurus, Suchomimus, and Irritator!
Baryonyx preyed on baby dinosaurs as well as fish.

beta.name: BETA
facts: Beta and Blue make a fierce mother-daughter duo. Beta is not only Blue's baby, she's also her identical clone. This is one team you don't want to mess with!
Not quite fully grown yet, Beta stands at just about 4 feet tall. Though she may still be young, Beta is already quick on her feet and shows little signs of fear.
Beta is already a strong hunter, but she's also rather clumsy. She's still learning to become a fearsome dinosaur like her mother.
Beta can already easily take down her prey, even occasionally going after animals as large as a full grown wolf!

big_eatie.name: BIG EATIE
facts: This Tyrannosaurus Rex shows a large quantity of scars gained from numerous fierce battles against other dinosaurs.
It was discovered that this dinosaur has surprising levels of intelligence, being able to recognize faces and individuals.
Her behavior is surprisingly aggressive and requires special protocols inside the Park.
Despite her aggressive tendencies, she showcases a nurturing side towards her children.

blonde_becky.name: BLONDE BECKY
facts: Blondie is the second Becklespinax twin, sister to Brunette!
Becklespinax are able to peacefully coexist with herbivore dinosaurs, as long as they have distinct territories.
The Becklespinax will defend its territory fiercely from other carnivores, becoming highly aggressive towards other dinosaurs threatening its environment!
Becklespinax have incredible stamina, and therefore can chase their prey for long periods of time, exhausting them in the process.

blue.name: BLUE
facts: Blue is a fiercely loyal Velociraptor, making conscious decisions about where her loyalties lie. This is in contrast to most other dinosaurs, who act on instinct.
Blue's distinct markings come from the DNA of a Black-throated monitor lizard. Her unique blue stripe is also how she got her name.
As a baby, Blue fought with her sister Echo, resulting in a scar on her lip. After this battle, Blue established herself as the Alpha of the pack.
Blue has proven capable of expressing compassion and pain, a unique ability for a dinosaur. She's empathetic and highly intelligent compared to other Velociraptors.

bonitasaura.name: BONITASAURA
facts: Did you know that Bonitasaura gets its name from the fossil quarry La Bonita? It means 'pretty lizard' in Spanish.
At 30 feet in length, the Bonitasaura is quite small compared to its sauropod cousin, the Argentinosaurus.
With a square jaw, the Bonitasaura's blade-shaped teeth are ideal for shearing vegetation.
The Bonitasaura lived in the woodlands of South America during the Late Cretaceous Period some 65 million years ago!

borealopelta.name: BOREALOPELTA
facts: Borealopelta means 'Northern Shield.'
Borealopelta was discovered in Alberta, Canada in 2011!
This ankylosaur is remarkable for the large bony spikes that protrude from its shoulders.

The Borealopelta specimen was discovered in the Millenium Mine in Alberta, in an area where only marine fossils had been discovered previously. It is believed this Borealopelta specimen may have washed out to sea after death.

brachiosaurus.name: BRACHIOSAURUS
facts: Brachiosaurus' front legs are longer than its hind legs, and its name means 'arm lizard'.
The long neck of the brachiosaurus contains a system of large air sacs that may have helped and improve breathing efficiency.
Like most sauropods, Brachiosaurus is very social and thrives in herds.
This massive creature can grow up to 50 feet tall and was once thought to be the largest of dinosaurs. Size is the only defense it needs!

brontotherium.name: BRONTOTHERIUM
facts: Brontotherium, also called the Megacerops, is a giant hoofed mammal similar to a rhinoceros. It stands at nearly 8 feet tall!
Though it resembles a massive rhinoceros with two nose horns, Brontotherium is actually more closely related to horses!
The horns of males Brontotherium are larger than those of the female. This is because Brontotherium duel for their mates!
Brontotherium means 'Thunder Beast.' The name certainly suits the gigantic armored herbivore!

brunette.name: BRUNETTE
facts: Brunette is one of two Becklespinax twins!
Becklespinax are a genus of theropod dinsoaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Becklespinax resemble a mixture of the powerful features of the T. rex and body of the Spinosaurus!
Becklespinax are remarkable for their aquatic abilities, and have been known to be able to hold their breath for impressive amounts of time!

tyrannosaur_buck.name: BUCK
facts: This male T. rex was once hunted by the big game hunter Roland Tembo on Isla Sorna!
Tranquilized by Tembo and brought to San Diego, this T. rex escaped and was let loose in the city!
This Tyrannosaurus Buck is the father of Junior, a Tyrannosaurus fawn featured in 'The Lost World'!
This T. rex's escape was likely due to the amphetamine he was dosed with while in containment, putting him in a berserk state!

tyrannosaur_bull.name: BULL
facts: This Tyrannosaur was born in the InGen research facility at Isla Sorna.
This theropod, while still massive, is slightly smaller than other adult Tyrannosaurus.
Researchers have noted this Tyrannosaurus to be very territorial and eager to enter turf wars with other dinosaurs.
Bull is from the original group of Tyrannosaurs created by InGen, including Rexy, Buck, and Doe !

bumpy.name: BUMPY
facts: Bumpy’s horns are asymmetrical, with one being rounder and less blunt than the other, giving her a uniquely adorable appearance.
Bumpy is a particularly loyal Ankylosaurus, acting as a protector to those she has bonded with. This makes her an invaluable companion and friend.
Bumpy is roughly 60% the size of a normal ankylosaurus due to her shortened incubation period.
The armored shell and heavy club at the end of her tail provide Bumpy with protection from any potential enemies.

carbonemys.name: CARBONEMYS
facts: This giant turtle, with its 5.5 foot-long shell, lived at the same time as other giant reptiles such as the Titanoboa.
The Carbonemys name means "coal turtle" because the first fossil was discovered in a coal mine in Colombia.
The ridge on the upper shell suggests that Carbonemys' neck was too long to retract fully, so it tucked its head to the side.
The skull remains suggest that the Carbonemys' jaw was strong enough to bite through armored crocodiles, but the fossil record is inconclusive.

carnoraptor.name: CARNORAPTOR
facts: While smaller than its cousins, the Carnoraptor can still do some damage with its 3 inch long claws!
Weighing in at just over 500 pounds, or the size of a grizzly bear, this raptor is surprisingly light on its feet.
Moving at speeds upwards of 35 miles per hour, the Carnoraptor will charge its prey, impaling them with its horns!
Meaning 'meat-eating thief', the Carnoraptor is the ultimate predator. Its 6 inch claws are rivaled only by the Velociraptor!

carnotaurus.name: CARNOTAURUS
facts: Discovered in 1984, the Carnotaurus is best known from a single skeleton found in the Argentinian Chubut Province.
Did you know that of all the carnivorous bipedal dinosaurs, the Carnotaurus is the only one to have horns?
Carnotaurus is Latin for 'meat-eating bull,' due to its bull-like horns.
The modern Carnotaurus created by InGen has chameleon-like camouflage which it uses to ambush its prey!

carnotaurus_toy.name: CARNOTAURUS TOY
facts: InGen scientists brought this creature to life by combining dino DNA with the sturdiest toy-grade materials ever made.
Despite its size, it is surprisingly lightweight, and its multi-jointed legs make it one of the fastest chargers around.
Its signature horns have been specially reinforced, making them formidable weapons in any head-on clash.
The Carnotaurus sometimes hunts by freezing completely still for an ambush, making it look like an ordinary object.

cearadactylus.name: CEARADACTYLUS
facts: The wingspan of the Cearadactylus is estimated to be between 4 and 5.5 meters. Since only the skull of the Cearadactylus has been discovered, the wingspan is estimated by comparing to other pterosaurs.
The Cearadactylus fossil was not dug out by a dedicated research team, but was instead purchased from fossil dealers in Italy in 1983!
Several mistakes were made in the rebuilding of the Cearadactylus fossil, including mistaking the front of the lower jaw for the snout, and enlarging the teeth.
The Cearadactylus skull was eventually reconstructed properly, discovering that it had smaller teeth then previously thought, as well as a crest present on the snout.

ceratosaurus.name: CERATOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that the Ceratosaurus' name means 'horned lizard' because of the horn on its nose?
Like the Ankylosaurus, what makes the Ceratosaurus unique is its dermal armor!
Ceratosaurus fossils have been found in Utah and Colorado. They date back to the Late Jurassic Period, 145 million years ago!
Estimated to weigh roughly 2000 lbs, the Ceratosaurus weighs as much as a polar bear!

ceratosaurus_toy.name: CERATOSAURUS TOY
facts: InGen scientists brought this creature to life using dino DNA, giving it a wilder roar than any Ceratosaurus before it.
Its flexible, movable joints let it strike lifelike poses and launch into action at a moment's notice.
The distinctive horn on its snout is its pride and joy — perfect for intimidating rivals before a mega chomp attack.
When it attacks, its markings seem to light up with excitement, dazzling prey just before its ferocious jaws snap shut.

cerazinosaurus.name: CERAZINOSAURUS
facts: The Cerazinosaurus is a hybrid of Therizinosaurus and Ceratosaurus, two predators that may have lived up to 100 million years apart!
Cerazinosaurus, or 'horn rake lizard,' takes its name from the Ceratosaurus's sharp horn and the raking claws of the Therizinosaurus!
Created by Ingen, the Cerazinosaurus has both feathers and scales, inherited from each of its "parents"!
The forelimbs of the Cerazinosaurus are more flexible than those of the Ceratosaurus. An inheritance from the long-armed Therizinosaurus!

cervalces.name: CERVALCES
facts: The Cervalces is a deer from the Pleistocene time period with features that strongly resemble that of a moose.
Cervalces has been primarily found in areas that suggest a natural habitat of mires and wetlands.
Natural predators of the Cervalces may include the grey wolf, dire wolves, and brown bears.
Along with most of the rest of the North American megafauna, Cervalces disappeared at the end of the Pleistocene time period.

charlie.name: CHARLIE
facts: Charlie is the youngest of Owen's raptor pack.
Charlie's green color pattern comes from the Iguana DNA infused within her genome.
Charlie is famous for taking down several InGen troopers in the Jurassic World escape incident.
Like her sisters, Charlie became subservient to the Indominus Rex as a pack leader during the Jurassic World escape incident!

chromaspinus.name: CHROMASPINUS
facts: The Chromaspinus was created by Jurrasic Park scientists genetically splicing DNA from Spinosauruses with that of Parasaurolophuses.
Chromaspinus has inherited Spinosaurus' back crest as well as Parasaurolophus' skull crest.
Jurassic Park scientists weren't sure whether to feed Chromaspinus fish or plants, so they tried both and found it liked both.
Chromaspinus' love of fish and plant material was discovered when a lab tech lost their sushi lunch to the juvenile dinosaur.

coloborhynchus.name: COLOBORHYNCHUS
facts: Did you know that the Coloborhynchus species was first defined in 1874 by Richard Owen?
Coloborhynchus earned its name, 'maimed beak', from the damaged condition of a fossil found in the nineteenth century.
The Coloborhynchus has a keel-shaped crest on the front of its jaws. It's broad, thinning from the base to the top of its head!
The Coloborhynchus has two forward pointing teeth, three pairs of teeth pointed to the sides, and a final two pointed downward.

compsognathus.name: COMPSOGNATHUS
facts: At approximately 125 centimeters long, the Compsognathus is one of the smaller dinosaurs currently known.
Experts were able to confirm the Compsognathus was a carnivore when a small lizard was found inside the dinosaur remains!
The Compsognathus have digitigrade feet, meaning they would balance on their toes rather than their feet.
The Compsognathus have particularly large eyes, suggesting it was a visually orientated predator. It likely would have needed quick reflexes to prevent prey from escaping.

compsognathus_gen_2.name: COMPSOGNATHUS GEN 2
facts: Compsognathus was discovered as an almost complete skeleton in 1859 in Bavaria, Germany then a second was found in France in 1971.
The size of the Bavarian skeleton made it believed to be chiken-sized, but now it's thought as a juvenile, making it much bigger!
While it's thought Compsognathus preyed on small vertebrates, an hungry pack could hunt bigger creatures!
For decades, Compsognathus was the smallest known non-avian dinosaur, but Microraptor and Mahakala were discovered later.

compsognathus_jp2.name: COMPSOGNATHUS JP2
facts: The Compsognathus lived during the Late Jurassic period, roughly 150 million years ago. That means it lived in the same time period as the Stegosaurus!
In The Lost World, Compsognathus are cute pack hunters. Keep in mind that even the smallest of dinosaurs are dangerous in large groups!
Compsognathus means 'elegant jaw' in Greek. This tiny dinosaur is known for its graceful appearance!
Compsognathus have been a staple of Jurassic Park and Jurassic World movies since their first appearance, they are in almost all of them !

compsoraptor.name: COMPSORAPTOR
facts: Compsoraptors will feed constantly on small game, such as critters and insects, and will share the spoils of their hunts among themselves.
It has been discovered that the Compsoraptors communicate with one another using those low-pitched sounds, organizing and cooperating as a pack.
Analysts observed the cranial composition of the Compsoraptor can emit low-pitched sounds, unperceivable by human ears.
This InGen creation inherits considerable claws from its hybrid DNA, making it especially lethal against its usual prey.

compsovenator.name: COMPSOVENATOR
facts: Compsovenator depend on coordinated attacks to take down much larger targets!
Compsovenator resemble Compsocaulus with the cranial frills of the Dracovenator!
The display functions of Compsovenator indicate the communication abilities these tiny predators use to coordinate group behaviour.
It is believed that the size of Compsovenator frills indicate their relative dominance among conspecifics.

concavenator.name: CONCAVENATOR
facts: The Concavenator is a usually solitary creature, but it is known to congregate at the carcasses of larger dinosaurs.
Even though Concavenator has large claws, it uses its mouth for most of its attacks.
Concavenator is one of many predatory dinosaurs - including Spinosaurus - to have raised spines on its back.
Concavenator has bristles on its arms, just like a cat, that allow it to better detect and manipulate prey between its claws.

corythosaurus.name: CORYTHOSAURUS
facts: The first Corythosaurus was discovered in Red Deer River, Alberta in 1912!
Did you know that the Corythosaurus belongs to a 'duck-billed' family of dinosaurs called hadrosaurids?!
Its name, Corythosaurus, means 'helmet lizard'. It comes from the shape of its skull, which resembles a hard hat.
Some Corythosaurus fossils were lost in WWI. In 1916, a Canadian ship carrying fossils bound for England was sunk by the Germans!

cryolobourgiania.name: CRYOLOBOURGIANIA
facts: The Cryolobourgiania has a distinct head shape, making it easy to identify no matter the distance.
The Cryolobourgiania has a smaller wingspan than the Arambourgiania, though they are no less powerful!
Just like the Cryolophosaurus, the Cryolobourgiania has a unique facial crest used to attract a mate.
The Cryolobourgiania has an exceptionally large mouth, allowing it to scoop up small prey as it flies by with ease.

cryolophosaurus.name: CRYOLOPHOSAURUS
facts: Cryolophosaurus lived in the Jurrasic tropical forest that is now Antarctica.
Cryolophosaurus is one of the earliest meat eaters we have ever discovered.
Cryolophosaurus' interesting face crest was probably used to identify other members of its species, or to attract mates.
Before being named 'Cryolophosaurus', this dinosaur was referred to by the nickname 'Elvisaurus' due to the similarity of its crest to a pompadour.

dakoderma.name: DAKODERMA
facts: Dakoderma means 'biting skin.' The name suits this spiky creature!
Dakoderma can use its shell for protection against larger predators.
Dakoderma is slightly longer and much heavier than its genetic ancestor Dakosaurus.
Jurassic World staff theorize this carnivorous hybrid would feed on its genetic ancestor Dakosaurus if given the chance.

dakosaurus.name: DAKOSAURUS
facts: Meaning ‘biter lizard’, the Dakosaurus gets its name from its large, serrated teeth.
Most marine crocodiles ate a fish-based diet, but Dakosaurus’s skull and jaws indicate it was a predator of larger prey.
Spending most of its time at sea, the crocodilian Dakosaurus has developed flippers and a fluke-like tail.
Reaching upwards of 15 feet in length, the Dakosaurus is twice as long as Shaquille O’Neil is tall!

dakotaraptor.name: DAKOTARAPTOR
facts: Traces of the Dakotaraptor are dated to the very end of the Mesozoic Era, making it one of the last dromaesosaurids in history.
While it possesses wings, these are vestigial and not flight-capable, much like modern large birds such as the ostrich and emu.
Each toe of a Dakotaraptor's foot claw evolved to serve different purposes, making it akin to prehistoric utility knife.
While closely related to the Utahraptor, the Dakotaraptor evolved in a pursuit-type predator with long legs rather than an ambush predator.

darwinopterus.name: DARWINOPTERUS
facts: Did you know that the Darwinopterus was named after biologist Charles Darwin? Its name means 'Darwin's wing'.
Like modern songbirds, the Darwinopterus flits between trees and long grass, searching for insects to eat.
Just like modern reptiles, the Darwinopterus eggs have soft, parchment-like shells!
The Darwinopterus has a wingspan of 3.3 feet, half that of an American bald eagle!

deinocheirus.name: DEINOCHEIRUS
facts: In 1965, a pair of large arms were discovered. They inspired the Deinocheirus's name, which means 'horrible hand.'
Nearly 40 years after discovering a pair of Deinocheirus arms, two complete specimens were discovered in 2014.
Did you know that the Deinocheirus belongs to a group of dinosaurs that resemble the modern ostrich?
The Deinocheirus has a small head, large eyes, long neck, and beak. They are among some of the fastest dinosaurs!

deinonychus.name: DEINONYCHUS
facts: The Deinonychus is a fast and agile hunter whose large brain allows it to perform intricate maneuvers while it hunts.
The tail of the Deinonychus is enclosed in a bundle of bony rods that helped it maintain balance.
The Deinonychus' principal weapon is its sickle-shaped talons on its hind feet.
Like modern birds, the Deinonychus' wrists were able to flex sideways, allowing it to grasp prey with more ease.

deinosuchus.name: DEINOSUCHUS
facts: The Deinosuchus' teeth are the size of bananas.
The Deinosuchus is probably the largest crocodylian ever in existence.
The Deinosuchus seems to have been an opportunistic predator, eating almost everything it could sink its giant teeth into.
Deinosuchus teeth marks have been found in Albertosaurus and Appalachiosaurus bones, proving that it even hunted living Tyrannosaurs.

deinotherium.name: DEINOTHERIUM
facts: Deinotherium is Latin for 'terrible beast.' This giant mammal is similar to modern elephants, but has a shorter trunk.
At fifteen feet tall and weighing 8-12 tons, Deinotherium is twice as heavy as a modern African bush elephant!
Like modern elephants, Deinotherium has a deceptively human-shaped skull. Fossil finds may have inspired medieval myths of bipedal giants!
Deinotherium may have been hunted by prehistoric relatives of modern man. Their bones are often found together in arachaeological sites!

delta.name: DELTA
facts: Delta is a highly trained Velociraptor, fiercely loyal to her pack leader, Owen Grady. She responds quickly to his commands and plays a crucial role in the pack's coordinated hunts.
Delta is easily recognizable by her greenish-blue scales and piercing yellow eyes, giving her a striking appearance compared to the other raptors in the pack.
Delta displays remarkable intelligence, able to strategize and adapt during hunts. Her sharp instincts make her one of the most effective members of the raptor squad.
Among the raptors, Delta shares a particularly strong bond with Owen, often being one of the first to respond to his cues, showcasing her deep connection with her trainer.

diabloceratops.name: DIABLOCERATOPS
facts: Named for the dual spikes emerging from the top of its crest, Diabloceratops means 'devil-horned face.'
Diabloceratops was first discovered at the Wahweap formation in Kane County, Utah.
Diabloceratops measured 15 feet in length and weighed over a ton!
Diabloceratops is probably more closely related to Nasutoceratops than other Centrosaurs like Sinoceratops ot Centrosaurus.

dilophoboa.name: DILOPHOBOA
facts: Don't let this hybrid near the thermostat! Its preferred temperature is approximately 90 °F.
Titanoboa likes to prey on aquatic creatures, while Dilophoboa hunts mainly on land.
This hybrid has more vertebrae than Titanoboa, allowing it to better support its massive body when traveling on land.
Dilophoboa is a venomous constrictor. It can spit poison halfway across the average American basketball court!

dilophosaurus.name: DILOPHOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Jurassic World's Dilophosaurus are smaller than their ancestor, have a neck frill, and paralyzing venom?
The Dilophosaurus gets its name, 'double-crested lizard', from the two distinct crests on top of its head.
The first Dilophosaurus fossils were discovered in 1942 in Arizona. Of three skeletons, two were taken to Berkeley.
It's believed that the frog DNA or a splicing error may have caused the abnormal traits in InGen's clones.

dilophosaurus_gen_2.name: DILOPHOSAURUS GEN 2
facts: This Gen 2 is the product of a geneticist's failed attempt to replicate the splicing error that created the first Dilophosaurus clone.
Dilophosaurus Gen 2 likes to fish. Like a racoon, it wades in water, using the digits on its front feet to feel for its prey.
The Dilophosaurus Gen 2 has a high pitched call, like an eagle. The original has a lower call, similar to that of an owl.
A mature Dilophosaurus Gen 2 will develop sharp spines on its neck frill. The anatomy of its frill is similar to that of a porcupine fish.

dimetrocarnus.name: DIMETROCARNUS
facts: As its name suggests, Dimetrocarnus is a carnivorous creature!
While shaped like a Dimetrodon, this superhybrid is as vicious and cunning as the Carnoraptor!
The bright blues and reds of this creature's skin grow more distinct as the creature matures.
Like the Dimetrodon, it is believed Dimetrocarnus's sail helps in both mating displays and heat regulation.

dimetrodon.name: DIMETRODON
facts: Biosyn is famous for researching and engineering pelycosaurs like the Dimetrodon. These prehistoric reptiles lived 50 million years before the dinosaurs.
Did you know that the Dimetrodon is more closely related to mammals than dinosaurs?
The Dimetrodon is best identified by its distinctive sail, which may have evolved to regulate its body temperature!
Dimetrodon's have a 'locked-in' limb orientation, which causes them to be splay-legged and walk like a crocodile.

dimorphodon.name: DIMORPHODON
facts: Did you know that the Dimorphodon clones created for Jurassic World are known to chirp like birds?
Dimorphodon is Greek for 'two-form tooth' because they had two kinds of teeth. InGen's clones only have one.
Clones of the Dimorphodon tend to have a blue-ish gray body with pink on its face.
Did you know that the Dimorphodon are great climbers? They have large, curved claws and a low center of gravity.

diplocaulus.name: DIPLOCAULUS
facts: Did you know that Diplocaulus means 'double caul'? This salamander-like amphibian has a boomerang-shaped skull.
Diplocaulus fossils have been discovered in rock dating back from the Permian period in North America and Morocco.
Like the Dimetrodon, the Diplocaulus is not actually a dinosaur, but a type of primitive amphibian!
Outside of Jurassic World's living zoo, there are only two Diplocaulus specimens on display; both are in the United States!

diplocaulus_gen_2.name: DIPLOCAULUS GEN 2
facts: Diplocaulus means 'double caul,' referring to the membranes on each side of its head!
Diplocaulus lived during the Late Carboniferous in current day North America and Africa.
The bright green Diplocalus GEN 2 grows brown stripes as it evolves.
Many functions for Diplocaulus' 'horns' have been proposed, including protection of gills and locomotion!

diploceraspis.name: DIPLOCERASPIS
facts: Diploceraspis lived in North America during the Permian period, which was the last period of the Paleozoic Era.
The Diploceraspis very closely resembles the Diplocaulus, though they differ in size, with Diploceraspis measuring smaller.

The Diploceraspis is a genus of lepospondyl amphibian, a type of early tetrapod. As a lepospondyl, the Diploceraspis likely had spool-shaped vertibrae that grew as bony cylinders around the notochord.
The Diploceraspis was originally recognised as two species: D.burkei and D.conemaughensis. However, this was proven inaccurate due to the size range overlap.

diplodocus.name: DIPLODOCUS
facts: The Diplodocus is one of the largest known dinosaurs. From the tip of its tail to its nose, it is 175 feet long!
Much of the Diplodocus' length is attributed to its neck and tail. Its tail, in particular, has 80 vertebrae, where the neck only has 15.
Did you know, compared to other large sauropods, the Diplodocus is actually quite trim? It weighs between 20-25 tons!
Over eleven museums across the world have a Diplodocus on display!

diplosuchus.name: DIPLOSUCHUS
facts: Diplosuchus means "double crocodile." The name suits this extra-aggressive crocodilian hybrid!
Diplosuchus is more agile on land than most crocodilians due to its slightly longer legs.
Diplosuchus rarely digs its own burrows. Instead, it steals them from other swamp dwelling creatures!
Diplosuchus is sometimes observed sharpening its claws. The behavior suggests high intelligence.

diplotator.name: DIPLOTATOR
facts: Did you know that Diplotator means 'double irritation?'
Unlike its stocky relative, the Diplocaulus, the Diplotator weighs a staggering 2 tons! That's more than an adult Giraffe!
Like modern whales and dolphins, the Diplotator swims up and down. Its legs are too short to propel its body through deep water!
Unlike the Diplocaulus and Irritator, the Diplotator has spikes on its head and a spiky tail!

diprotodon.name: DIPROTODON
facts: Diprotodon is the largest marsupial to ever live. It looks like a giant Australian wombat!
Though it's as big as a rhino, the Diprotodon's closest living relatives are the koala and wombat!
Aborginal tribes of Australia have interpreted the bones of Diprotodon as those of the mythological monster 'the bunyip'!
Diprotodon went extinct around the time humans arrived in Australia. It's possible we hunted them to extinction.

dodo.name: DODO
facts: The Dodo was native to the island of Mauritius, east of Madagascar in the Indian ocean.
The Dodo was first described by Europeans during the Second Dutch Expedition to Indonesia in 1598.
After European arrival on the island of Mauritius, the Dodo was hunted to extinction by humans and invasive species. It went extinct around 1662.
Today, the Dodo remains a prominent symbol of the importance of conservation and the human capacity to quickly destroy entire species!

tyrannosaur_doe.name: DOE
facts: This female T. rex is the mate of Tyrannosaur Buck, a powerful male T. rex hunted by Roland Tembo.
Tyrannosaur Doe is the mother of Junior, an adolescent Tyrannosaur featured in The Lost World!
Tyrannosaur Doe can be distinguished from her mate by her brownish hue.
Determined to protect her little son, This T-Rex mother is prepared to face any danger, even risking her own life to shield him!

doedicurus.name: DOEDICURUS
facts: An ancestor to modern armadillos, this armored mammal stands 5 feet tall and has a spiked tail it uses like a mace!
Doedicurus is a glyptodont, a prehistoric family of giant armadillos. In fact, it's the largest glyptodont to ever live!
Fossils of some Doedicurus shells show fractures consistent with their tails! This means they duelled each other!
It's possible Doedicurus store energy and liquid inside a hump under their dome, just like a modern camel!

dolichorhynchops.name: DOLICHORHYNCHOPS
facts: Did you know that Dolichorhynchops means ‘long-nosed face’? It gets its name from its long snout!
The Dolichorhynchops has long, thin teeth and a powerful bite which it uses to capture fish.
Because the Dolichorhynchops swallowed its prey whole, it also would swallow small stones to aid with digestion.
At 10 feet in length, the Dolichorhynchops is smaller than an average car!

draco_lux.name: DRACO LUX
facts: The Draco Lux is a nocturnal herbivore, hunting while other dinosaurs are asleep!
With a large beak, the Draco Lux is a forager, digging and searching for its next meal. It can easily shatter shells and nuts of all sizes.
The full bioluminescent capacities of Draco Lux only appear when it is threathened or excited.
The bioluminescence of the Draco Lux is used as a warning sign and defensive mechanism against nocturnal predators.

dracoceratops.name: DRACOCERATOPS
facts: Don't get in Dracoceratops' way! It's known to have one of the most powerful ramming attacks in Jurassic World.
This hybrid's name means "horn faced dragon."
Unlike most herbivores, Dracoceratops are known to pick fights with nearby predators!
Dracoceratops typically travel in pairs and will huddle together at night when temperatures drop.

dracorex.name: DRACOREX
facts: This herbivore has leaf-shaped teeth, which are perfect for chewing foliage.
Dracorex means "Dragon King". Its head is circled in spikes, like a crown.
The spikes that protrude from Dracorex’s skull prevent predators from attacking it head-on.
The identity of Dracorex is heavily debated by paleontologists. Some believe it is a juvenile Pachycephalosaurus.

dracorex_gen_2.name: DRACOREX GEN 2
facts: Dracorex variants are known for their distinctive skull, which features spiky horns and a long muzzle, giving it a dragon-like appearance.
The shape of Dracorex's skull resembles mythical dragons, which is how these variants get their name meaning "dragon king."
Despite its fierce appearance, Dracorex GEN 2 is an herbivore, feeding on low-lying plants and shrubs by using its beak-like mouth to clip vegetation.
Dracorex GEN 2 is a Pachycephalosaur, a group of dinosaurs known for their thick, bony skulls. However, unlike others in its family, Dracorex GEN 2 has a flat, rather than domed, skull.

dracovenator.name: DRACOVENATOR
facts: Dracovenator is a carnivorous theropod. It preys on smaller dinosaurs and other animals.
Dracovenator lived during the Early Jurassic period, around 200 million years ago, making it one of the early large predators in its ecosystem.
Dracovenator is characterized by a distinctive bony crest on its head, similar to those found in other early theropods. This crest may have been used for display or species recognition.
Fossils of Dracovenator were discovered in South Africa, specifically in the Elliot Formation, which has yielded many important dinosaur fossils from the Early Jurassic period.

dreadactylus.name: DREADACTYLUS
facts: Despite using Dreadnoughtus DNA, the Dreadactylus is rather small. It is, however, one of the largest flocks registered by InGen.
The small wings of the Dreadactylus do not impede it's flight abilitles. On the contrary, it makes this dinosaur much more agile in the air.
Its tail has a complex structure of vertebrae, allowing it better balance both on the ground and in the air.
The Dreadactylus is a very social creature, staying in large flocks.

dreadnoughtus.name: DREADNOUGHTUS
facts: The Dreadnoughtus is a Herbivore that lived in South America during the Cretaceous period. It is a huge creature, measuring 85 feet in length and weighing approximately 49 metric tons.
The Dreadnoughtus is one of the largest terrestrial vertebrates ever discovered. It is calculated to have the greatest mass of any land animal currently known.
The discovery of the Dreadnoughtus has helped provide information about the size and anatomy of other giant titanosaurian sauropods, in particular their limbs, hips, and shoulders.
The shoulder blade, hip bone and forearms of the Dreadnoughtus are proportionately longer than any other known titanosaur. This is one big beast!

dsungaripterus.name: DSUNGARIPTERUS
facts: Discovered in 1964 in China, the Dsungaripterus gets its name from the Junggar Basin where it was found.
The Dsungaripterus has a low bone crest running from the base of its skull to about halfway down its beak!
Did you know that the Dsungaripterus has the wingspan of 10 feet, the same as a modern trumpeter swan?
Together, the neck and head of the Dsungaripterus is roughly 3.3 feet long!

dunkleosaurus.name: DUNKLEOSAURUS
facts: Though Dunkleosaurus may look like a fish, it actually has lizard DNA from its ancestor Mosasaurus!
Like the Mosasaurus, Dunkleosaurus breathes air and must surface to fill its lungs!
The larger fins of the Dunkleosaurus make it a stronger swimmer than the Mosasaurus.
The powerful bite of the Dunkleosaurus allows it to feed on armored aquatic creatures, just like its ancestor Dunkleosteus.

dunkleosteus.name: DUNKLEOSTEUS
facts: Did you know that the Dunkleosteus is named after David Dunkle, curator of the Cleveland Museum of Natural History?
Much of the Dunkleosteus is covered with bony plates, providing protection from other predators--including fellow Dunkleosteus!
The Dunkleosteus doesn't actually have teeth. Its beak-like mouth is full of sharp, bony plates!
Reaching 33 feet in length, the Dunkleosteus is not a particularly fast swimmer. It relies on ambush tactics to snare its prey.

echo.name: ECHO
facts: Echo is one of the four Raptors trained by Owen Grady at Jurassic World!
Echo is green with distinctive orange striping.
Early in life, Echo competed with her pack-mate Blue for dominance of the Raptors!
As the two youngest Raptor siblings, Echo and Charlie are often together!

edaphosaurus.name: EDAPHOSAURUS
facts: Edaphosaurus has a distinct sail on its back, giving it a larger, more intimidating look to predators.
The name Edaphosaurus means "pavement lizard", a reference to the arrangement of the teeth in its mouth.
The Edaphosaurus has a surprisngly small head, especially when compared to its body, though it compensates with a strong, robust jaw.
The teeth of the Edaphosaurus resemble small pegs, capable of grinding plants into a paste before being swallowed.

edestus.name: EDESTUS
facts: Known as the ‘scissor-tooth shark’, the Edestus’ teeth resemble pinking shears!
Did you know that the Edestus belongs to the same family as the Helicoprion? They even share the same unique dental structure!
The Edestus can grow up to 20 feet in length, the size of a modern great white shark!
Unlike modern sharks, the Edestus does not shed its serrated teeth. Instead, they are worn down over time.

edmontosaurus.name: EDMONTOSAURUS
facts: The Edmontosaurus is named for the city in Alberta, Canada where it was first discovered.
The Edmontosaurus has the most numerous fossil records of any dinosaur ever discovered.
This duck-billed Dinosaur has a wattle on top of its head! This is a fleshy crest, like that of a chicken.
The bones in the tail of the Edmontosaurus were reinforced with tendons that became ossified with age.

einiosaurus.name: EINIOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Einiosaurus means 'forward curving horn' on account of the shape of the horn on its nose?
Unlike other herbivores at Jurassic World, the Einiosaurus prefer to travel in single-species herds.
The Einiosaurus weighs roughly 1 ton. That's the same as a full grown polar bear!
When a herd of Einiosaurus are threatened, they form a defensive circle around their young. Just like elephants!

elasmosaurus.name: ELASMOSAURUS
facts: The Elasmosaurus, one of the best known plesiosaurs, is named after the Greek word elasmos, meaning 'thin plate'.
A relatively slow swimmer, the Elasmosaurus hides itself in the darker depths and uses its long neck to ambush schools of fish.
The Elasmosaurus lives its life entirely underwater. But instead of laying eggs like a turtle, it incubates an egg internally!
While early fossils constructions suggested it coiled its neck like a snake, the Elasmosaurus actually holds its neck straight!

elasmotherium.name: ELASMOTHERIUM
facts: Did you know that Elasmotherium means ‘thin plate beast’? It’s also known as the ‘Giant Rhinoceros of Siberia’!
Reaching the size of an adult Mammoth, the Elasmotherium has a large, thick horn on its forehead.
The Elasmotherium uses its horn for multiple functions, which include attracting mates, foraging, and digging for water.
Like the Woolly Rhinoceros, the Elasmotherium has a thick, wool-like coat, which insulates it from its colder habitat.

entelodon.name: ENTELODON
facts: Meaning ‘complete teeth’, the Entelodon gets its name from the number of teeth it has!
Despite having a pig-like head, the Entelodon is actually closely related to hippos and whales!
Fast on its feet, this pig-like mammal can give a horse a run for its money!
Did you know that the Entelodon has a 2 foot long skull, and is 4.4 feet tall at the shoulders?

entelorhacos.name: ENTELORHACOS
facts: Entelorhacos has the strongest jaw of any terror bird hybrid.
The mammalian DNA of this hybrid gives it a stronger sense of smell than most avian creatures.
Unlike other terror birds, Entelorhacos does not have hollow bones. This makes it heavier and slower than some of its competitors.
The muscular density of this hybrid usually gives it the edge over creatures like Phorusrhacos in battle.

eolambia.name: EOLAMBIA
facts: Due to gaps in the fossil record, the exact size of Eolambia remains uncertain. Estimates of its size range from 18 to 29 feet!
So far, every Eolambia fossil has been found in Utah, USA!
Eolambia means 'Dawn Lambeosaurine.' The second half of its name comes from the paleontologist that first studied Lambeosaurine fossils, Lawrence Lambe.
The Eolambia is part of a large group of dinosaurs called 'Hadrosauroidea.' This means Eolambia is related to the Iguanodon through a common group of ancestors, the Hadrosauriformes!

eremotherium.name: EREMOTHERIUM
facts: Eremotherium is a 20 foot sloth! Unlike its modern relatives, it walks on the ground instead of hanging from tree branches!
Eremotherium existed on earth for over 4 million years, living all across what is now North and South America!
The Eremotherium lived all the way to the end of the Pleistocene. It only died out 11,000 years ago!
Eremotherium differs from the sloth, its modern descendent, in that it only has one claw on each foot!

erlikosaurus.name: ERLIKOSAURUS
facts: The Erlikosaurus is the only segnosaurian to be discovered with a complete skull!
Discovered in 1972, the Erlikosaurus was found at Bayshin Tsav in Mongolia.
Did you know that the Erlikosaurus is named after a mythological demon king, Erlik, from Mongolian mythology?
The mythological demon king, Erlik, is known as the god of death and underworld in Mongolia. It's an odd choice for an herbivore.

erliphosaurus.name: ERLIPHOSAURUS
facts: The carnivorous Erliphosaurus combines DNA from the herbivore Erlikosaurus and the crested carnivore Dilophosaurus!
As the Erliphosaurus ages, spines begin to grow from the back of its head. At full maturity, these turn into its impressive fringe!
The fringes of the Dilophosaurus are purely for show. But the hardier Erliphosaurus uses its fringes for defense in battle as well!
The Erliphosaurus is among the most colorful dinosaurs in Jurassic World! It uses its bright color as distraction in battle!

eryops.name: ERYOPS
facts: Though an amphibian, Eryops is also an ancestor of modern mammals! It was one of the first reptiles to walk on land!
Eryops lived around 295 million years ago. At 1.5-2 meters, it was one of the biggest land animals of its time!
Lucky enough to have discovered a naturally mummified specimen, paleontologists have actually handled the Eryops's skin!
Did you know that Eryops means 'drawn out face' because its eyes were so far back in its skull?

eucladoceros.name: EUCLADOCEROS
facts: Eucladoceros means "bush antlered deer." It is named for its widely splayed antler pattern.
Eucladoceros is large for a deer, only slightly smaller than a modern moose!
The incredible antlers of Eucladoceros split into 12 different tines.
Eucladoceros evolved in the Early Pleistoscene era and spread across Europe, the Middle East and Asia.

eudimorphodon.name: EUDIMORPHODON
facts: The Eudimorphodon was actually quite small, only weighing about 20 pounds!
Nearly complete skeletons of this ancient pterosaur have been found perfetly preserved in shale.
Like many modern birds, the Eudimorphodon is an excellent fisherman. It has teeth perfect for grabbing its prey from the water!
Eudimorphodon means 'true dimorphic tooth', referring to the strong differentiation of its teeth from each other.

euoplocephalus.name: EUOPLOCEPHALUS
facts: Like the Ankylosaurus, the Euoplocephalus has armored eyelids and bone plate armor.
Did you know that the Euoplocephalus weighs 2 tons? That's more than a Porsche 911!
This heavily armored beast has a pair of defensive horns poking from the back of its neck.
The name Euoplocephalus is Greek for 'well-armed head', due to this dinosaur's thick body armor!

fukuimimus.name: FUKUIMIMUS
facts: The Fukuimimus, much like the Fukuisaurus, has a low kinetic skull, giving it a powerful bite force useful to crush nuts from trees.
While classified as an herbivore, the Fukuimimus is an opportunistic omnivore. It will eat whatever they happen to forage to supplement their plant-based diet.
The Fukuimimus retains the powerful legs of the Struthiomimus and is able to run at speeds of around 50 km/h.
The shape of the Fukuimimus's forward limbs resemble hooks and are used to grasp at tree branches in order to gather food.

fukuisaurus.name: FUKUISAURUS
facts: The Fukuisaurus gets its name from "Fukui", a Prefecture of Japan, where the first remains of the Fukuisaurus were discovered.
Though the Fukuisaurus is similar to other ornithopods, it appears to be more primitive than others of this group.
The Fukuisaurus was approximately 4.3 meters long, which is roughly the same length as an adult female giraffe is tall!
The Fukuisaurus was initially discovered from skull fragments alone, so experts use other similar dinosaurs for the reconstruction of the rest of the body.

gallimimus.name: GALLIMIMUS
facts: The Gallimimus clones created by Masrani Global Corporation are a foot taller than the originals created by InGen!
Gallimimus, which is Latin for 'chicken mimic,' gets its name from its ostrich-like skeleton.
Did you know that the Gallimimus can run up to 60 mph? That's as fast as a modern cheetah!
The InGen Gallimimus variety ranged in color, from bright orange and dark red patterns to peach and brown with purple stripes.

gastornis.name: GASTORNIS
facts: The massive head and razor sharp beak of this large flightless bird pack quite a peck!
Often thought to be a predator, these massive land birds actually feed mostly on plants and seeds!
Standing at more than 6 feet tall, Gastornis lays eggs bigger than that of any modern bird!
Scientists have found Gastornis bones, eggs, feathers, and even footprints. That's amazing, considering the bird lived 40 million years ago!

geolasmosaurus.name: GEOLASMOSAURUS
facts: The coloring of this hybrid helps it camouflage in reed-filled environments.
Geolasmosaurus is an ambush hunter, snatching prey with its claw-like jaws.
The slow movements of Geolasmosaurus's frilled fins can be hypnotic to prey and predators, stunning them before this hybrid attacks.
As Geolasmosaurus matures, its vision gets worse. However, its more rigid spines help it sense movement.

geosaurus.name: GEOSAURUS
facts: The Geosaurus, meaning ‘Mother of Giants lizard’ is named after the Greek ‘Ge’, who was the mythical mother of giants!
Did you know that the Geosaurus has a short snout with serrated teeth? It preys on large fish and other marine reptiles.
Like modern crocodiles, the Geosaurus ambushes its prey! It hides in murky water and waits for the perfect moment to strike.
Although an ancestor of modern crocodiles, the Geosaurus only grew up to 10 feet in length. That’s smaller than today's crocs!

geosternbergia.name: GEOSTERNBERGIA
facts: Geosternbergia is also known as the Pteranodon sternbergi.
Geosternbergia was discovered in 1952 by paleontologist George F. Sternberg.
Among the largest pterosaurs, the wingspan of this flyer can reach up to 6 meters!
The most distinctive characteristic of Geosternbergia is its upright cranial crest.

gerrothorax.name: GERROTHORAX
facts: The name Gerrothorax means 'wicker chest!'
The flat body of the amphibious Gerrothorax probably allowed it to hide beneath the sands and mud of lake bottoms, awaiting prey!
Gerrothorax measured roughly 1 meter, and is known from a single specimen discovered in Thailand.
Some studies suggest Gerrothorax opened its mouth by lifting the top part of its head, like the lid of a box!

ghost.name: GHOST
facts: Ghost is an Atrociraptor, though along with the rest of her pack, she was likely bred using modified Velociraptor DNA as well.
Exceptionally savage, particularly cruel, and bred for extreme speed, Ghost is considered the perfect weapon.
Ghost was created to track and hunt anyone marked with a red laser. Once marked, the target will be relentlessly chased by Ghost and her pack.
Ghost gets her name from her white coloring. The stripes down her back and her vicious red eyes give her an extra menacing look.

giant_orthocone.name: GIANT ORTHOCONE
facts: The Giant Orthocone is related to squids and octopi. Like them, the Orthocone grabs prey with its tentacles and devours it with its beak!
The Giant Orthocone has very primitive eyes. Luckily, it lives in very deep water, where its keen sense of smell serves it better!
The Giant Orthocone has tentacles, but no suction cups. Instead, its eight arms are lined with smooth pads.
Orthocone means 'chambered horn'. This comes from the animal's most distinct aspect: its giant protective shell!

gigakylocephalus.name: GIGAKYLOCEPHALUS
facts: This ankylosaurid hybrid is more agile with its tail than many other ankylosaurs.
Gigakylocephalus's sharp club can inflict slicing wounds on opponents as well as blunt force damage.
Unlike other ankylosaurs, Gigakylocephalus uses its facial spike to ram opponents.
The facial spike of the Gigakylocephalus helps it forage for root matter to eat as well as providing a defensive weapon.

giganocephalus.name: GIGANOCEPHALUS
facts: Did you know that Giganocephalus is a misnomer? Its name means 'giant head', when in fact it actually has a small head!
The Giganocephalus has smooth, armored plates and four large spikes protecting its neck and shoulders.
Like the Euoplocephalus, the Giganocephalus has fused bone plates, protecting its back and neck from attack.
The Giganocephalus is nearly twice the size of its Euoplocephalus progenitor; weighing 4.2 tons and measuring up to 30 feet in length!

giganotosaurus.name: GIGANOTOSAURUS
facts: The Giganotosaurus is one of the largest known land-based carnivores - a perfect engineering project for Biosyn.
Giganotosaurus means 'giant southern lizard'. It lived in modern Argentina roughly 97 million years ago!
The Giganotosaurus is one of the genetic templates used in creating the fierce Indominus rex!
A Giganotosaurus bite is three times less powerful than a Tyrannosaurus Rex's. Still strong enough to snap you in half though!

giganotosaurus_gen_2.name: GIGANOTOSAURUS GEN 2
facts: The Giganotosaurus Gen 2 has extremely powerful legs, allowing for particularly fast movements despite her huge size.
Giganotosaurus Gen 2 is a little bit gentler than the Giganotosaurus, despite her slightly larger size. She is still a fearsome beast, though, so watch out!
The Giganotosaurus and the Giganotosaurus Gen 2 have the largest skull among all currently known theropods.
The modifications used by Jurassic World's geneticists increased the jaw strength of the Giganotosaurus Gen 2, resulting in a much more terrifying bite!

gigantophis.name: GIGANTOPHIS
facts: Before Titanoboa was discovered, Gigantophis was considered the largest snake to ever live.
Gigantophis can grow up to around 7 meters (21 feet) or more!
Gigantophis lived 40 million years ago in the Sahara region.
Gigantophis was so big it may have preyed on the ancestors of modern-day elephants!

gillicus.name: GILLICUS
facts: Gillicus was a 6 foot prehistoric fish - a huge catch by today's standards, but tiny in its own time!
Gillicus were often eaten by their larger relative Xiphactinus. We know this because we have found fossils of Gillicus inside this creature!
Gillicus eat small fish but also filter feed, meaning they suck in plankton like whales suck in krill!
At only 6 feet, Gillicus has to watch out for the mega-sharks and Mosasaurs that share its waters!

gillirhynchops.name: GILLIRHYNCHOPS
facts: Gillirhynchops has a number of sharp teeth in its mouth that partially serve to filter plankton.
Gillirhynchops swallows small stones to act as Gastroliths to help break down fish that it swallows whole.
Gillirhynchops sucks fish into its mouth with a vacuum-like suction. The second function of its hooked teeth is to prevent escape.
This dinosaur was created by dna samples taken from a single source: a Dolichorynchops fossil with a juvenile Gillicus preserved in its stomach.

glyptodon.name: GLYPTODON
facts: This ancestor of the modern armadillo looks almost exactly like one, except it's the size of a small car!
Glyptodon were discovered as early as 1823. It's bones were initially mistaken for those of a Megatherium, the giant ground sloth!
Glyptodon, meaning 'grooved tooth', was named for the unique grinding shape of its teeth.
Glyptodon were reserve eaters. This means they required much less food to survive than other herbivores!

glythronax.name: GLYTHRONAX
facts: The dark coloring of the Glythronax makes it an effective night hunter.
The Glythronax shares all of the aggresive qualities of the 'gore king' Lythronax.
The armor of the Glythronax helps it muscle competitors off fallen prey.
Glythronax can be observed ramming prey as well as using its jaws.

gorgosaurus.name: GORGOSAURUS
facts: A full grown Gorgosaurus weighs over 4000 pounds!
Gorgosaurus is the best represented tyrannosaurid in fossil records. Scientists have discovered dozens of unique specimens!
Gorgosaurus is one of the faster tyrannosaurids. Before InGen, paleontologists discovered this by analyzing their femurs and tibias!
Gorgosaurus means terrible or fierce lizard in Greek. It certainly suits the 30 foot powerhouse!

gorgosuchus.name: GORGOSUCHUS
facts: Did you know that the Gorgosuchus is a distant relative to the Tyrannosaurus rex?!
Combining the strongest traits of a Gorgosaurus and Kaprosuchus, the Gorgosuchus's name means 'dreadful crocodile'!
Measuring at 6700 pounds per square inch, the force of a Gorgosuchus bite rivals a modern saltwater crocodile!
The Gorgosuchus is an exclusively terrestrial predator, preferring to hunt a range of smaller ceratopsids and hadrosaurs.

goronyosaurus.name: GORONYOSAURUS
facts: Goronyosaurus is a marine lizard that belongs to the mosasaur family.
A small mosasaur, Goronyosaurus could reach a length around 5.15 meters (17 feet), around the length of a large female great white shark!
Goronyosaurus fossils have been discovered in The Dukamaje Formation of Niger and Nigeria.
Goronyosaurus' unique teeth seem designed for smashing food, with unknown effects on the Goronyosaurus' diet.

gryposuchus.name: GRYPOSUCHUS
facts: Gryposuchus resembles the modern day Gharial, a piscivorous crocodile with a remarkably long body and narrow snout.
This ancient crocodile is believed to have survived in both saltwater and freshwater.
Gryposuchus lived amongst other equally massive ancient crocodiles during the Miocene, but was likely the only one to be exclusively piscivorous.
Gryposuchus could grow up to 32 feet in length, which is almost double the length of the Nile crocodile!

guanlong.name: GUANLONG
facts: Did you know that its name, Guanlong, is derived from Chinese? It translates to 'five colored crowned dragon.'
The Guanlong earns its name from the crest on its skull and the colorful badlands of Wucaiwan, where its fossils were first found.
Standing at 3.3 feet tall, the Guanlong is just shy of 10 feet in length!
Did you know the Guanlong lived 92 million years before the T. rex? Unlike other tyrannosaurs, it has three long fingers on its hands!

haast_eagle.name: HAAST EAGLE
facts: The Haast Eagle is the large eagle known to have ever existed !
Scientists hypothesize it evolved to such a massive size in order to adapt to its favorite prey : the flightless moa.
Studies of the Haast Eagle's evolution indicate it morphed into this form extremely fast, suggesting the environment was very welcoming to this type of physical adaptation.

Despite its size, its wings are shorter than one might expect. Scientists explain this by changes in mode of flight, favoring maneuvering in dense forest environment rather than high-altitude soaring.

hainosaurus.name: HAINOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Hainosaurus means ‘lizard from Haino’ which is located in Belgium? It was named by Louis Dollo in 1885!
Feeding on turtles, smaller mosasaurs, plesiosaurs, fish, and sharks, the Hainosaurus has even been known to eat birds!
Closely related to the Tylosaurus and Taniwhasaurus, the Hainosaurus is rivaled only by the Mosasaurus!
At 40 feet in length, the Hainosaurus is one of the largest mosasaurs to have roamed prehistoric oceans!

hatzegopteryx.name: HATZEGOPTERYX
facts: Did you know that Hatzegopteryx fossils were first discovered in Transylvania, Romania?
Hatzegopteryx, which means 'Hateg basin wing,' is named for the small town of Hateg near where its fossils were discovered!
Did you know that Hateg in the Hunedoara County, while far inland, was once an island during the Cretaceous Period?
The Hatzegopteryx has a wingspan of nearly 40 feet! The only dinosaur to rival it is the Quetzalcoatlus!

hauffiosaurus.name: HAUFFIOSAURUS
facts: The first Hauffiosaurus was discovered in the Posidonia shale formation in the 19th century.
Though Hauffiosaurus was discovered almost 200 years ago, it was not recognized as a new species until 2001!
Hauffiosaurus is classified as a medium sized plesiosaur, measuring about 11 feet (3.5 meters) long.
The long thin snout of the Hauffiosaurus is rare amoung plesiosaurs.

helicoprion.name: HELICOPRION
facts: Greek for ‘spiral saw’, Helicoprion gets its name from the shape of its teeth, which are called ‘tooth whorls’.
This prehistoric shark can grow up to 33 feet in length, making the Helicoprion one of the largest ocean predators of its time!
Did you know that the Helicoprion shares many skull features with the modern goblin shark?
At 24 inches long, the Helicoprion’s tooth whorl stumped scientists. Early guesses placed it on the dorsal fin and even the tail!

henodus.name: HENODUS
facts: Did you know that Henodus means ‘single tooth’? It gets its name from the single tooth located on either side of its mouth.
The Henodus, which resembles a turtle, is actually a placodont: an extinct type of marine reptile that includes plesiosaurs!
The Henodus has weak limbs. Because of this, it spends most of its life in the water, feeding on vegetation.
The Henodus’s shell is composed of many bones that form a mosaic pattern. This bony armor is fused to its spine.

homalocephale.name: HOMALOCEPHALE
facts: Homalocephale is a pachycephalosaurid species discovered in 1974.
Homalocephale has a flat, wedge shaped skull.
It is the shape of Homalocephale's skull that gave it its name, which means 'even head' in Greek.
Homalocephale's wide pelvis may be to birth live young or protect from headbutts to the flank!

hyaenodon.name: HYAENODON
facts: Hyaenodon means 'Hyena Tooth,' but the two species aren't related. While hyenas are related to cats, Hyaendon is a creodont.
The Hyaenodon is such a powerful predator that it preys on other carnivores! A common meal is the Nimravid, or 'false saber-toothed cat!'
In the back of its mouth, the Hyaenodon has razor sharp teeth designed for slicing. This allowed it to cut its meat and digest faster!
Like a wolf, Hyaenodon tracked prey by scent. It could even idenify weak and sick animals by their smell!

hydraboa.name: HYDRABOA
facts: The Hydraboa is named for the serpentine monster slain by Heracles in ancient Greek myth!
Scientists named this creature the Hydraboa for its unique molting patterns. Hydraboa's head and neck grow brighter each time the snake molts, as if the creature were growing a new head!
Hydraboa has a serpentine body, with characteristics reminiscent of both Dilophoboa and Edestus, featuring a sleek, elongated form and vibrant, reptilian scales.
Hydraboa combines the power of its constricting abilities and powerful fangs in its attacks.

hynecoprion.name: HYNECOPRION
facts: The Hynecoprion is a very large fish with a unique facial feature.
The 'tooth whorl' of the Helicoprion appears in a modified, yet gigantic version in the Hynecoprion.
The result of this mashup is a saw-toothed shark that can (sort of) walk on land. Nightmare Fuel!
Hynecoprion's fins can be used as primordial legs, allowing it limited access to land.

hyneria.name: HYNERIA
facts: About 8 feet in length, the Hyneria is named for a town near where it was found: Hyner, Pennsylvania!
The powerful fins of the Hyneria mean it may have been able to crawl around on land for brief periods!
At a maximum of around 12 feet, Hyneria preyed on many smaller fish, including sharks!
The only fish related to Hyneria bigger than it was the Rhizodus, which measured up to 18 feet!

ichthyostega.name: ICHTHYOSTEGA
facts: Did you know that its name is Greek for 'fish roof'? The Ichthyostega has lungs as well as gills!
The Ichthyostega has a mixture of amphibious and fish-like features, including webbed feet and a fin on its tail!
Although its head resembles that of a fish, the Ichthyostega's long body and legs allow it to walk on land!
At 5 feet in length, an adult Ichthyostega is as long as a modern boomslang!

iguanodon.name: IGUANODON
facts: Iguanodon is one of the few creatures that can move as a quadruped and a biped.
Iguanodon was the second species to be scientifically labeled a dinosaur.
Iguanodon's teeth are very similar to the modern day Iguana’s, which it was named after.
Many groups of Iguanodon tracks have been excavated from Late Jurassic deposits, proving that the creature travelled in herds.

iguanosuchus.name: IGUANOSUCHUS
facts: This dinosaur's name means 'iguana-toothed-pseudo-crocodile' and it shows.
The Iguanosuchus' claws are 4x longer than those of a Grizzly bear: long enough to rip through sheet metal with relative ease.
Anyone unwise enough to climb into this Dinosaur's enclosure looking to take selfies riding it, will be sorely disappointed by the dismemberment that results.
There is only one food that will suffice for this ravenous hybrid: meat.

indominus_rex.name: INDOMINUS REX
facts: Did you know that the name Indominus rex means 'fierce' or 'untamable king'?
The birth of the Indominus rex was achieved by genetically modifying existing DNA in the Hammond Creation Lab.
The Indominus rex's roar can reach an estimated 140-160db – the same level as a 747 taking off and landing!
The distinct head ornamentation of the Indominus rex is an ultra-tough bony osteoderm that protects the cranium from attackers!

indominus_rex_gen_2.name: INDOMINUS REX GEN 2
facts: An experiment conducted to better understand the Indominus rex’s predatory instinct resulted in this equally dangerous Gen 2.
This apex predator’s preferred meal is Apatosaurus.
The Indominus rex Gen 2 is able to communicate with the Gen 2 creatures it was hybridized with.
The cuttlefish DNA added to this hybrid makes it a master of camouflage.

indoraptor.name: INDORAPTOR
facts: This fusion of the Indominus rex and Velociraptor is possibly one of the most intelligent dinosaurs to ever exist.
At a height of 7.3 meters and weighing nearly a metric ton, this dinosaur still manages to be light on its feet.
Among all of its other unique attributes, the Indoraptor also has the ability to echolocate!
One handler nicknamed the Indoraptor 'the stealth fighter jet of dinosaurs!'

indoraptor_gen_2.name: INDORAPTOR GEN 2
facts: The Indoraptor Gen 2 is always alert and has nearly perfect echolocation, making it impossible to ambush.
This superhybrid is easily aggravated and will swifty decimate creatures infringing on its territory, even after it has been fed.
