Herbivores inhabiting the area the Indoraptor Gen 2 is known to roam have begun to show heightened levels of anxiety.
The difference of coloring between the Indoraptor Gen 2 and the original is said to be the result of the alternative DNA used when creating the Gen 2.

indricoceros.name: INDRICOCEROS
facts: The prehensile lip of this hybrid allows it to grip and strip tree branches like a modern day giraffe.
The antlers of the Indricoceros can grow even larger than those of the Megaloceros.
Indricoceros means 'Indric horn.' In Russian folkore, the Indric beast is the king of all animals! It resembles a rhinoceros.
Indricoceros are observed dueling much less than their ancestor Megaloceros.

indricotherium.name: INDRICOTHERIUM
facts: Did you know that Indricotherium is a synonym of Paraceratherium? They’re both the same animal!
Paraceratherium means 'near the hornless beast', in reference to a similar species, Aceratherium.
The Indricotherium is massive, weighing up to 44,000 pounds! At its shoulder, it is nearly 16 feet tall!
Giraffe-like in build but more robust, the Indricotherium's prehensile upper lip allows it to graze on tall foliage.

irritator.name: IRRITATOR
facts: Irritator describes the way scientists felt when an altered skull fossil required many hours of restoration.
It is unknown where the Irritator was discovered as its fossils were collected illegally by fossil dealers.
Its full name is Irritator challenger, which is derived from Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's character, Professor Challenger.
Did you know that the Irritator is a close cousin to the Spinosaurus and share skull features?

irritator_gen_2.name: IRRITATOR GEN 2
facts: This pale Irritator may have developed its unique coloring to camouflage in a grassland environment.
This spinosaurid is mostly piscivorous, feeding on fish!
Both Irritator and Irritator GEN 2 are closely related to Spinosaurus, Suchomimus and Baryonyx!
More research is required on this GEN 2 creature to find out its differences from the original Irritator.

juggernaut_32.name: JUGGERNAUT 32
facts: This genetically modified Triceratops is one of the biggest and most dangerous creatures in Jurassic World.
Juggernaut 32's horns and armor plates make it a truly formidable enemy in battle.
Though an herbivore, it would still be a terrible idea to enter this dinosaur's territory.
If you manage to dodge the horns, you might still find yourself trampled beneath its powerful feet.

junior.name: JUNIOR
facts: Junior is a Tyrannosaurus fawn, that means he is not fully grown and is still learning how to hunt on his own.
Junior is the offspring of the Tyrannosaur Buck and Doe featured in "The Lost World"! This shows that the dinosaurs on Isla Sorna were a naturally breeding population.
Junior was captured by the big game hunter Roland Tembo when he was only a few weeks old but freed by Sarah Harding and Nick Van Owen.
Junior's first prey was Peter Ludlow, the CEO of Jurassic Park: San Diego at the end of the movie.

kaiwhekea.name: KAIWHEKEA
facts: Kaiwhekea is a plesiosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous.
The single known Kaiwhekea specimen was found nearly complete in Kaitiki formation in New Zealand!
Unlike some other plesiosaurs, Kaiwhekea has very small and numerous teeth. They are thought to have helped it catch small, fast prey.
Kaiwhekea means 'squid eater' because paleontologists believe these creatures were a staple of its diet.

kaprodacthylus.name: KAPRODACTHYLUS
facts: This flying Boar-croc is one of the last things you want descending on you from the treetops.
Created by splicing Tupandachtylus and Kaprosuchus genes, this dinosaur has the highest concentration of teeth to be found in the sky.
The jaws of the Kaprodacthylus are ridged. Without these ridges, this dino's teeth would prevent its mouth from closing.
This dinosaur specializes in diving for its food, like a king-fisher.

kaprosuchus.name: KAPROSUCHUS
facts: Did you know that its name means 'boar crocodile'? The Kaprosuchus has unusually large, tusk-like teeth that resemble a boar!
Like Homo sapiens, the Kaprosuchus has forward-facing eyes, meaning its field of view overlaps.
An adult Kaprosuchus can grow to 20 feet in length, twice the length of a modern crocodile!
The Kaprosuchus has enlarged, relatively straight, and sharp-edged teeth. This indicates that it's a terrestrial predator!

kaprosuchus_gen_2.name: KAPROSUCHUS GEN 2
facts: This ancient crocodile has 3 sets of teeth! 2 rows on the top and 1 on the bottom.
Kaprosuchus and Kaprosuchus Gen 2 have holes in their jaw bones where teeth from the opposite side of the mouth can insert, allowing their mouths to close completely.
This Gen 2 hunts on land, and its comparatively long crocodile legs allow it to charge prey with impressive momentum.
Kaprosuchus Gen 2 has a more rustic pigmentation than the original, making it an efficient hunter in any desert landscape.

kelenken.name: KELENKEN
facts: This 'terror bird' stands taller than the average human. Most scientists suggest it could reach up to 10 feet in height!
Kelenken has an odd claim to fame. With a skull measuring more than 2 feet, it has the largest head of any known bird.
The enormous beak of the Kelenken helps it to take down prey with powerful pecks.
Kelenken is a relative of the Phorusrhacos. It is one of the 18 Phorusrhacidae, or terror birds, that have been discovered so far.

kentrosaurus.name: KENTROSAURUS
facts: Adult Kentrosaurus' measure around 15 feet in length and weigh over 1.1 tons!
Like the Stegosaurus, the Kentrosaurus has a double row of small plates running down its neck and back and a spiked tail.
Did you know that the Kentrosaurus has a long spine on each shoulder? Its name means 'pointed lizard'.
The Kentrosaurus prefers a lush environment to sustain its diet of low growing vegetation.

koolasaurus.name: KOOLASAURUS
facts: Its name means 'Kool's lizard,' but the hyper-specialized Koolasaurus is anything but laid back!
Super cool only begins to describe this Hammond Creation Lab stroke of crocodilian genius, which can weigh up to 1,100 pounds!
With a diet largely consisting of aquatic creatures, the Koolasaurus's wide mouth has been known to snap up more than just fish.
Sporting the heavy armor of its crocodile descendants, the Koolasaurus overshadows their length at 25 imposing feet!

koolasuchus.name: KOOLASUCHUS
facts: Did you know the Koolasuchus gets its name from paleontologist Lesley Kool? It's also a play on the word 'cool'.
The Koolasuchus lived in Australia during the Early Cretaceous Period. Back then the climate in that area was much cooler!
It's believed the Koolasuchus hibernated due to the cool climate, explaining why it outlived its northern ancestors.
Similar in build to a crocodile, the Koolasuchus has a round head with tabular horns at the back of its skull!

koreanosaurus.name: KOREANOSAURUS
facts: Koreansaurus was first discovered in 2003, in the Boseong province of South Korea!
Koreansoaurus was a small dinosaur, reaching only roughly 2 meters in length.
The small Koreanosaurus is a burrowing dinosaur, using its large frontal claws to dig its den in the ground!
Two separate specimens of this herbivore have been discovered by paleontologists.

kronosaurus.name: KRONOSAURUS
facts: The Kronosaurus is named after the Greek titan, Kronos. It means ‘lizard of Kronos’!
Did you know that the Kronosaurus is an incredibly fast swimmer? Its powerful pectoral girdle supports very strong strokes.
At 33 feet long, and weighing 11 metric tons, the Kronosaurus is one of the largest plesiosaurs!
As an apex predator, the Kronosaurus eats in a similar fashion to the modern crocodile, clamping onto its prey with its jaws!

labyrinthodontia.name: LABYRINTHODONTIA
facts: Did you know that it's believed that the Labyrinthodontia is the progenitor of all modern amphibians?
Labyrinthodontia is Greek for 'maze-toothed.' It's named for the way each of its conical teeth forms!
With gills and primitive lungs, the Labyrinthodontia can live in water with low oxygen levels!
Like their modern frog descendants, the Labyrinthodontia lay eggs in the water, which then hatch into tadpoles!

labyrinthosaurus.name: LABYRINTHOSAURUS
facts: Like the Labyrinthodontia, the Labyrinthosaurus has strong, folded teeth made of enamel and dentin. Its name means 'maze lizard'.
Although not as large as the Argentinosaurus, the Labyrinthosaurus is still classified as a titanosaur, weighing over 85 tons!
The Labyrinthosaurus has a strong set of lungs as well as a swim bladder; an internal gas-filled organ which allows it to keep its head submerged underwater!
Did you know that the Labyrinthosaurus prefers a water-based environment, feeding on aquatic vegetation?

leedsichthys.name: LEEDSICHTHYS
facts: Leedsichthys has over 40,000 teeth within its massive jaws! What a dental record!
Though enormous, the Leedsichthys mostly fed on plankton, filtering it through its gills!
It is likely this filter-feeder grew large as a defense against the many predators in the Jurassic seas!
It's possible Leedsichthys was preyed on by smaller carnivorous sea creatures like Liopleurodon or Metriorhynchus.

leptocleidus.name: LEPTOCLEIDUS
facts: Did you know that Leptocleidus means ‘slender clavicle’? Its name comes from its shoulder bones.
The Leptocleidus prefers grassy, fresh water over open lakes. As a piscivore, it primarily eats fish.
Like other plesiosaurs, the Leptocleidus is capable of giving birth to live young.
An adult Leptocleidus can reach 10 feet in length, with a shorter neck than its plesiosaur relatives.

leptostega.name: LEPTOSTEGA
facts: This armored plesiosaur feeds on shellfish and squid.
Leptostega means 'slender roof.' It's a fitting name for this sleek but shelled sea creature!
In later evolutions, the shell of the Leptostega develops sharp points to repel predators.
The tail of the Leptostega has to be incredibly strong in order to propel its heavy, shelled form.

leucistic_baryonyx.name: LEUCISTIC BARYONYX
facts: The Leucistic Baryonyx is a genetically modified version of the Baryonyx.
Contrary to the Baryonyx, the Leucistic variant does not have eyes. However, its senses of smell and hearing are magnified ten times over!
Leucistic Baryonyx prefers cave habitats, where it uses its echolocation to silently stalk its prey!
The Leucistic Baryonyx is much paler than the traditional Baryonyx since it prefers closed environments such as caves and caverns.

limnorhynchus.name: LIMNORHYNCHUS
facts: The Limnorhynchus' name means 'marsh beak', referencing its preferred diet of fish and small amphibians!
The Limnorhynchus has spikes running from the tip of its beak to the tip of its tail!
At 75 pounds, the Limnorhynchus weighs the same as an adult Labradoodle!
Did you know that the Limnorhyncus is an amphibian? It can dive up to depths of 40 feet!

limnoscelis.name: LIMNOSCELIS
facts: A reptile-like amphibian, Limnoscelis is Greek for 'marsh-footed.'
Due to their stubby legs, which limit mobility, the Limnoscelis tend to hunt slow-moving prey.
The Limnoscelis are actually quite light, weighing between 5 and 10 pounds. That's the same as a house cat!
Did you know that despite their light build, the Limnoscelis are actually quite large, at 4 feet in length?

liopleurodon.name: LIOPLEURODON
facts: Ancient Greek for ‘smooth-sided teeth’, the Liopleurodon earns its name from the state of its teeth!
Did you know that the Liopleurodon can grow to be 23 feet long and weigh 3000 pounds?
An apex predator of the Jurassic seas, the Liopleurodon has eight-inch teeth making for a powerful bite!
The Liopleurodon has an awesome sense of smell. Just like a shark, it can smell blood, and it uses this sense to ambush prey!

liosichtodon.name: LIOSICHTODON
facts: Unlike Leedsichthys, Liosichthodon feeds on fish and squid as well as plankton.
Liosichthodon's large jaws help it swallow prey whole.
The mottled spots of the Liosichthodon continue to develop as it ages.
The spikes of the Liosichthodon help it defend against other oceanic predators, and muscle in on scavenged meals.

little_eatie.name: LITTLE EATIE
facts: This Tyrannosaurus Rex's colors appear much closer to others of her specie, and doesn't seem to have inherited the hue of her mother.
While still young, this dinosaur has almost reached maturity in terms of size.
This dinosaur still exhibits dependent behavior, showcasing that while it has reached physical maturity, it is still in a transitory period between childhood and adulthood.
Her hunting habits still developing seems to suggest a lot of what was attributed to instinct is, in fact, learned behavior through both trial-and-error and social interactions.

lythronax.name: LYTHRONAX
facts: Lythronax lived 79-80 million years ago on a prehistoric island continent called Laramidia.
Lythronax means "gore king" or "king of gore."
Lythronax is a tyrannosaurid, related to the T. rex and Tarbosaurus.
Lythronax could grow up to 26 feet (8 m) tall or more!

major.name: MAJOR
facts: Much like others of it's species, Major is not a picky eater. It will even eat other Majungasaurus.
Major is not fond of water, and like others of its species, will prefer to walk and hunt on land.
Its horn is used for competition among other Majungasaurus in social situations rather than combat.
Every 56 days, Major grows a full new set of teeth to replace the old ones since it uses them to gnaw on bones.

majungasaurus.name: MAJUNGASAURUS
facts: The Majungasaurus gets its name from Mahajanga, a province in northwestern Madagascar where its fossils were discovered.
Did you know that genetic material of the Majungasaurus was used by InGen to create the Indominus rex?
Perhaps one of the features that make the Majungasaurus distinct is its single, round horn on the top of its head!
From the tip of its nose to the tip of its tail, the Majungasaurus is 25 feet long. A great white shark maxes out at 23!

mammotherium.name: MAMMOTHERIUM
facts: This hybrid's mammoth fur makes it more suited for snow than its ancestor Elasmotherium.
The heavy horn and tusks of the Mammotherium require its neck and shoulders to be incredibly strong.
The Mammotherium's tusks help it uncover plant matter in frozen turf.
While this hybrid's tusks are ivory, its horn is keratin, just like a modern rhinoceros!

marsupial_lion.name: MARSUPIAL LION
facts: The Marsupial Lion actually isn't a lion at all - it's more closely related to wombats and possums!
At up to five feet tall, the Marsupial Lion is the largest carnivorous marsupial to ever live!
The Marsupial Lion went extinct 46,000 years ago - probably because humans were stealing all their prey!
The Marsupial Lion hunts Diprotodon and giant kangaroos, hiding its kill in trees like modern leopards!

masiakasaurus.name: MASIAKASAURUS
facts: Masiakasaurus is known for its distinctive forward-facing teeth, which are uniquely adapted for catching small prey like fish and insects, making it a specialized feeder among theropods.
This dinosaur is relatively small, measuring about 6 to 7 feet in length. Despite its size, Masiakasaurus is an agile and effective predator in its ecosystem.
Masiakasaurus lived in what is now Madagascar during the Late Cretaceous period, contributing to the island's rich and unique prehistoric fauna.
With a slender body and long legs, Masiakasaurus was likely a fast and nimble hunter, using its speed to chase down prey.

mastodon.name: MASTODON
facts: Though related, Mastodons and Mammoths are different creatures. One way to tell them apart is that Mastodons are slightly smaller than Mammoths.
During prehistoric times, Mastodons lived in large herds and preferred forest habitats.
The Mastodon went extinct around 10,000 years ago. Scientists believe this was likely due to over-hunting by humans!
The first Mastodon known to science was discovered in New York in 1705!

mastodonsaurus.name: MASTODONSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Mastodonsaurus means 'breast-tooth lizard'? It gets its name from its rows of conical teeth.
Fossils of the Mastodonsaurus were first identified in 1828. They have been found in Great Britain, Germany, and Russia.
Because the Mastodonsaurus has short limbs with poorly developed joints, it rarely leaves the swampy water of its habitat.
The Mastodonsaurus has a large, triangular-shaped head. Its head can reach up to 4 feet in length!

mauisaurus.name: MAUISAURUS
facts: The Mauisaurus was first discovered in New Zealand, and gets its name from the Maori mythical demigod, Maui.
Did you know that the Mauisaurus has one of the longest necks of the plesiosaurs? It has 68 cervical vertebrae!
At 26 feet long, the Mauisaurus has a slender body that allows for agile movement while swimming.
The Mauisaurus has sharp, jagged teeth which it uses to grip fish and squid. It’s even been known to hunt on the shoreline!

megaloceros.name: MEGALOCEROS
facts: Also known as the ‘Irish Elk’ and ‘Giant Elk’, Megaloceros is Greek for ‘Great Horn’.
With massive antlers and a massive build, the Megaloceros stands at 7 feet tall at the head!
Did you know that early human cave art depicts the Megaloceros to have a dark coat of fur with a white underside?
After breeding season has passed, the Megaloceros sheds its impressive antlers. But don’t worry, a new set will grow in!

megalocevia.name: MEGALOCEVIA
facts: The Megalocevia takes on a lot of traits from the Edaphosaurus from which it is created, such as prominent sail on the back.
As an excellent ambush predator, the Megalocevia is able to chase its prey into shallow waters easily using its tail and sail.
Megalocevia will often hide itself in murky waters, covering itself in mud as a means of camouflage.
As the Megalocevia ages, the distinct blue hues on its back and neck become more pronounced.

megalodon.name: MEGALODON
facts: Did you know that Megalodon means ‘big tooth’? This massive shark is 59 feet long!
The teeth of the Megalodon are the most common of its remains to be found. These teeth can reach up to 7 inches in length!
Sharing similar teeth serration, the Megalodon and modern white shark both bite down and shake their prey when attacking!
At four times the size of a great white shark, the Megalodon is much stockier, weighing up to 103 metric tons!

megalosaurus.name: MEGALOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that the Megalosaurus was the first dinosaur to be found? A fossil of its femur was discovered in the 17th century!
In 1677, Robert Plot described the first Megalosaurus fossil as a thighbone of a Roman war elephant or possibly a biblical giant!
Early reconstructions of Megalosaurus fossils depicted it as a quadraped, instead of a bi-pedal theropod!
The Megalosaurus prefers coastal regions, hunting along the beaches for resting plesiosaurs and scavanging tidal pools filled with fish.

megarchelon.name: MEGARCHELON
facts: Like the modern shark, this Aquatic hybrid continues to shed and grow teeth throughout its life!
As Megarchelon matures, its spots develop into armor plating.
The light blue patterns on the underbelly of the Megarchelon help it to camouflage in reflective water.
A fully mature Megarchelon can use its serrated skin for both offense and defense!

megatherium.name: MEGATHERIUM
facts: The Megatherium is also called the Giant Ground Sloth. It is one of the biggest mammals to ever live!
As one of the slowest and largest mammals in its ecosystem, the Megatherium has no reason to run from a predator!
Still around during the Holocene, Megatherium probably interacted with humans!
The average Megatherium, standing on its hind legs, can reach 20 feet in height! That’s the same as the Easter Island statues!

megistocurus.name: MEGISTOCURUS
facts: The shell over Megistocurus' back makes it nearly invulnerable to attacks from above.
Megistocurus sleeps 16 hours a day just like the armadillo, a relative of its ancestor Doedicurus!
The heavy shell of the Megistocurus makes it slower than other Cenozoic predators.
A fully mature Megistocurus is dangerous from almost every angle!

megistotherium.name: MEGISTOTHERIUM
facts: Like most Cenozoic meat-eaters, Megistotherium was most succesful during the Eocene Epoch, before it was displaced by more modern predators.
The name Megistotherium means both "greatest beast" and "bone crusher." This hyaenodontid weighed over 1000 pounds.
The Megistotherium is related to hyenas. In size, however, it is closer to a modern polar bear!
Megistotherium likely hunted Woolly Mammoths for food. Scientists believe this because they have found dislocated Mammoth bones grouped with Megistotherium fossils.

meiolania.name: MEIOLANIA
facts: Meiolania's name, which means "small roamer", likely came from the fact that it was originally thought to be a lizard. This deduction was due to the description of the fossil skull.
Meiolania is the largest known land turtle, with the biggest specimens estimated to be up to 250 centimeters long.
Meiolania had both a spiked head and spiked tail, which may have been used as a defense against predators.

Turtles are classed in two groups: one folds their necks under their spines, the other folds their necks to their sides. However, due to the spikes on its skull, the Meiolania can't do either, making it a bit of a turtle enigma.

metoposaurus.name: METOPOSAURUS
facts: Did you know Metoposaurus means 'front lizard'? It's name is derived from the way it scoops fish into its wide jaws!
Fossils of the Metoposaurus have been found in mass graves. It's believed that they died huddled together during a drought!
During the dry seasons, the Metoposaurus uses its forearms and flat head to burrow underground.
At 10 feet in length, an adult Metoposaurus weighs 1000 pounds. For contrast, a water buffalo weighs 1400 pounds!

metriacanthosaurus.name: METRIACANTHOSAURUS
facts: Did you know the Metriacanthosaurus is named for its vertebrae? It comes from the Greek metrikos, 'moderate', and akantha, 'spine'.
InGen's Metriacanthosaurus clones created for Masrani Global are a meter smaller than the original species!
The Metriacanthosaurus is taller than the Allosaurus, standing at 11 feet, but shorter than the Arcanthosaurus.
The first clones created by InGen were featherless, while current versions of the species have proto-feathers on their arms and spine!

metrialong.name: METRIALONG
facts: Did you know that Metrialong means 'moderate dragon'? It references its crocodilian snout, which is narrower and longer than average.
Weighing between 300 and 350 pounds, the Metrialong is stockier than its agile Guanlong progenitor!
Like the Metriorhynchus, the Metrialong's diet includes fish, amphibians, and other marine reptiles.
The Metrialong has a distinct fin-like tail, an under-developed sail, and long arms suited for swimming and hunting.

metriaphodon.name: METRIAPHODON
facts: Did you know that Metriaphodon means 'moderately formed tooth'? It has a primitive snap and hold method of feeding.
The Metriaphodon prefers a diet of small vertebrates, including lizards, rodents, and small animals.
Unlike the Dimorphodon clones, the Metriaphodon has a wingspan of 6 feet and can effortlessly glide short distances!
Size wise, the Metriaphodon can weigh up to 100 pounds. That's more than a German shepherd!

metriorhynchus.name: METRIORHYNCHUS
facts: Smaller and less well-armoured than other ocean predators, the Metriorhyncus relies on its agility in the water to avoid becoming prey itself!
The Metriorhynchus lay its eggs like turtles, coming to shore to bury their clutch in the sand!
This 500 pound, 10 foot long carnivore spends much of its life in salt water, hunting fish and other aquatic creatures.
Similar in size to a crocodile, the Metriorhynchus is designed for swimming, with a smooth body and a finned tail!

microposaurus.name: MICROPOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Microposaurus means 'small-eyed lizard'?
InGen's clones of the Microposaurus have rich, emerald mottling that allows them to blend into swamp water!
The Microposaurus's jaw, while not nearly as destructive as the SuperCroc, is lined with super sharp edged teeth.
This awe-inducing clone can reach lengths of 30 feet, although InGen scientists have predicted lengths of near 40!

monkeydactyl.name: MONKEYDACTYL
facts: Monkeydactyl has opposable thumbs that it uses to climb and hunt!
Monkeydactyl's scientific name is Kunpengopterus antipollicatus, from words meaning 'opposite' and 'thumb.'
The thumb of the monkeydactyl helps paleontologists understand the evolution of pterosaur flight.
Monkeydactyl has a wingspan of approximately 85 cm, or 2.8 feet.

monolophosaurus.name: MONOLOPHOSAURUS
facts: While their names are similar, the Monolophosaurus is actually not closely related to the Dilophosaurus!
Monolophosaurus means 'single-crested lizard.' Its name comes from the protrusion on the top of its head.
Discovered in 1981, the fossils of the Monolophosaurus were found in Xinjiang China by a Canadian-Chinese expedition!
Did you know that it is believed that the Monolophosaurus' characteristic crest evolved to attract potential mates?!

monostegotops.name: MONOSTEGOTOPS
facts: Fusion with carnivore DNA makes the Monostegotops more aggressive than its herbivore ancestors.
Monostegotops prefers to forage alone instead of in groups like the Triceratops or Stegosaurus.
Monostegotops' solitary behaviour may be due to its carnivore DNA.
Monostegotops is heavily armored and can inflict serious damage with its powerful charging attacks.

mortem_rex.name: MORTEM REX
facts: Mortem Rex's name means "Death King", a fitting name for such a fearsome creature.
This creature mutated and evolved much more than what was anticipated by InGen scientists, leading to its current appearance.
InGen scientists are still puzzled by the presence of dorsal spines on its back, as they are usually a defense mechanism against other predators.
It has been observed that the Mortem Rex possesses a specific territorial behavior, showcasing intelligence by tolerating other types of dinosaurs in its environment.

mosasaurus.name: MOSASAURUS
facts: Meaning 'Meuse lizard', the Mosasaurus earns its name from the Meuse River, where its first fossil specimens were discovered.
At 60 feet long, the Mosasaurus was one of the largest and last of the mosaurids to live.
The Mosasaurus hunts near the surface, preying on fish, birds, and anything else it can reach (including the Indominus rex)!
Discovered in the late 18th century, the Mosasaurus' skull was thought to belong to a crocodile or an unknown species of whale!

mosasaurus_gen_2.name: MOSASAURUS GEN 2
facts: Jurassic World’s geneticists modified their method of artificial size inflation since creating the Mosasaurus. The result is a Gen 2 similar in size, but with less bone density.
The Mosasaurus Gen 2’s lungs are a different shape than the original, allowing it to explore further below the water’s surface.
Due to their slower speed, massive size, and tendency to live in bales like other turtle species, Archelon is the most popular prey targeted by the Mosasaurus Gen 2.
The Mosasaurus Gen 2 has been observed to breach the water’s surface without reason. Experts speculate that this is a form of play.

mosasaurus_gen_3.name: MOSASAURUS REBIRTH
facts: Contrary to popular belief, the Mosasaurus doesn't hunt primarily by scent, but rather by sight !
The Mosasaurus was one of the apex predators of the Late Cretaceous period. Remains of Mosasaurus have been discovered across multiple continents.
The Mosasaurus's sight is so developped, it can see into the infrared and ultraviolet spectrum !
It evolved to have four different types of teeth in order to prey on a large variety of other dinosaurs.

mylodon.name: MYLODON
facts: Mylodon pelts contained bony parts that offered some protection against predators.
Mylodon remains found in cave deposits with human artifacts suggest people hunted them for food.
Mylodon's huge claws were probably most often used for digging, however it is not impossible it used them for defense as well.
Though it went extinct around the end of the last ice age, Mylodon is one of the few species thought by some to still be alive as a Cryptid.

nasutoceratops.name: NASUTOCERATOPS
facts: Did you know that Nasutoceratops means 'large-nosed horn-face'? It has large horns that resemble those of cattle!
The Nasutoceratops originally lived in the American Southwest, in what is now the state of Utah.
During the Late Cretaceous Period, the Nasutoceratops lived on a large floodplain in a wet and humid climate.
The Nasutoceratops has a large frill lined with low crescents of bone instead of spikes.

nodosaurus.name: NODOSAURUS
facts: Nodosaurus means 'Knobbed Lizard.'
Nodosaurus is a member of the family Ankylosauridae. This means it is related to the famous Ankylosaurus!
Unlike the Ankylosaurus, the Nodosaurus has no club on its powerful tail.
Nodosaurus fossils were first discovered in 1889 in Wyoming.

nundagosaurus.name: NUNDAGOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Nundagosaurus means 'predator river lizard'?
An adult Nundagosaurus can weigh up to 2.5 tons. That's nearly as much as a blue whale's tongue!
To support its incredible weight, the Nundagosaurus has muscular legs, as its back is heavily plated with protective spikes.
The Nundagosaurus's tail serves as additional defense as well as a counter weight to its body!

nundasuchus.name: NUNDASUCHUS
facts: Did you know that Nundasuchus means 'predator crocodile'?
While the original Nundasuchus was a terrestrial reptile, InGen's clones are amphibious, suited to a semi-aquatic lifestyle.
Jurassic World's Nundasuchus are excellent swimmers, preferring to ambush and drag their prey into the water like a crocodile.
Did you know that an adult Nundasuchus can reach over 9 feet in length? An American crocodile can grow up to 16 feet!

nyctosaurus.name: NYCTOSAURUS
facts: Nyctosaurus means night lizard, due to the resemblance of this creature to a bat!
Nycotosaurus is a Nyctosaurid, a family of pterosaurs specialized in soaring.
Nyctosaurus likely flew in a similar way to modern soaring sea-birds like the Albatross.
Nyctosaurus is native to the region of the Niobrara Formation in the mid-west of the United States. In the Cretaceous period, this region was a massive shallow sea that Nyctosaurus fed from!

omega_09.name: OMEGA 09
facts: InGEN denies any part in the creation of this T. rex, but has expressed interest in studying its battle habits.
This creature is highly combative and prefers to live in solitary.
The glow radiating from cracks in this creature's scales intensifies when it becomes agitated.
At 35 feet in length this creature is quite a bit smaller than Indominus rex.

onchopristis.name: ONCHOPRISTIS
facts: Did you know that Onchopristis means ‘giant saw’? It is named after its rostrum, which resembles a saw blade!
Resembling a massive, 26 foot long sawfish, the Onchopristis is actually more closely related to the modern ray.
The Onchopristis’ 8 foot rostrum is equipped with electrosensors, which it uses to sense nearby prey along the seafloor.
Sweeping the seafloor, the Onchopristis impales its prey on the barbed spikes that run down the edges of its rostrum!

one_armed_baryonyx.name: ONE-ARMED BARYONYX
facts: This dinosaur lost an arm while fighting others in underground combat rings.
This Baryonyx also has an impaired left eye from previous injuries in the combat rings.
Its prosthetic, while limited in motion, still sports a distinctive large claw used to battle.
Outside of fights, this dinosaur is not particularly aggressive and prefers peace and quiet.

one_eyed_allosaurus.name: ONE-EYED ALLOSAURUS
facts: This dinosaur recently obtained by InGen has only one functioning eye. This suggests it fights recklessly and has a bold temperament despite its wound.
Data from this dinosaur confirms that Allosauruses can hunt in groups, but do not have pack mentality.
This specimen also confirms that growth of the Allosaurus during its lifespan is uneven, requiring different hunting strategies depending on its body size, type and environment.
The Allosaurus skull houses room for specific glands used to excrete excess salt from its diet.

ophiacodon.name: OPHIACODON
facts: Meaning 'snake tooth', the Ophiacodon lived mainly in the swamps of North America during the Carboniferous Period!
Did you know Ophiacodon fossils have been found in England, France, Canada, as well as eight American states?
The Ophiacodon has massive but very precise jaws. It can snap up fish, insects, small reptiles and amphibians with ease!
Did you know that the Ophiacodon is one of the species in the evolutionary line leading to mammals?!

ophiacomimus.name: OPHIACOMIMUS
facts: Although this hybrid inherited a carnivorous set of teeth, its primary source of food is vegetation. The blades inside its mouth function as weapons rather than as utensils.
Ophiacomimus maintained the ostrich-like skeleton of the Gallimimus after its fusion, making it extremely fast.
Both creatures involved in this hybrid’s fusion contributed pigmentation genetics that make up the lively coloration on its back.
The crests on the back and chest of the adult Ophiacomimus function as fins underwater, allowing this land creature to retrieve aquatic plants that grow in deep rivers.

ophthacerapsis.name: OPHTHACERAPSIS
facts: The Ophthacerapsis has a similar head shape to the Diploceraspis, with a unique skull shaped like a boomerang.
Like the Ophthalmosaurus, the Ophthacerapsis does not lay eggs. Instead, she births her young via live birth, similar to a mammal.
The Ophthacerapsis has exceptional eyesight, allowing it to more easily spot predators both on land and in the sea.
Though they are small, the teeth of the Ophthacerapsis are incredibly sharp. This allows it to easily devour fish and large insects at mealtime.

ophthalmosaurus.name: OPHTHALMOSAURUS
facts: Ophthalmosaurus was the only ichthyosaur in the middle Jurassic through to the Cretaceous period.
Ophthalmosaurus gave birth to its young in live births, not by laying of eggs.
The Ophthalmosaurus derives its name from its eyes; the largest proportional eyes known among sea creatures of the late Jurassic period.
Ophthalmosaurus had large rings of eye bones which prevented damage from water pressure in the lower depths.

ornithocheirus.name: ORNITHOCHEIRUS
facts: Ornithocheirus’ snout is shaped like a rudder, and its mouth is full of sharp vertical teeth - great for catching fish!
This pterosaur has a total wingspan of about 20 feet. That's just a bit shorter than a school bus!
The skin on Ornithocheirus' wings connect to its legs, making it great at flying and terrible at walking!
Ornithocheirus can fly great distances. Its fossils have been discovered in South America and Europe.

orthacanthus.name: ORTHACANTHUS
facts: Did you know that Orthacanthus means ‘vertical spike’? It’s derived from the defensive spike on the back of its head.
A freshwater shark, the Orthacanthus has a long dorsal fin and an eel-like body.
The Orthacanthus can grow to be 10 feet long. That’s nearly as long as a great white shark!
The Orthacanthus hunts in murky swamps. Its double-fanged teeth are specialized for grappling with larger, more powerful prey!

ostafrikasaurus.name: OSTAFRIKASAURUS
facts: Fossils of the Ostafrikasaurus were first collected between 1909 and 1925 in Tanzania, East Africa.
Its name, Ostafrikasaurus, is derived from the continent in which it was found: Africa.
Did you know that the Ostafrikasaurus has sharp, serrated, two inch long teeth?
Classifying the Ostafrikasaurus has been tough. If related to the Spinosaurus, it will be the earliest example in the fossil record!

ostaposaurus.name: OSTAPOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that the Ostaposaurus means 'East Africa-eyed Lizard'?
Preferring a diet of fish and amphibians, the Ostaposaurus has been known to target smaller dinosaurs that approach the water's edge.
The head of the Ostaposaurus is significantly smaller than its Microposaurus progenitor.
The jaws of the Ostaposaurus are lined with 1 inch long serrated teeth, ideal for tearing meat!

oviraptor.name: OVIRAPTOR
facts: The Oviraptor's name means "egg thief". This is a misnomer, as it seems the first Oviraptor discovered was not stealing eggs, but protecting her own nest at the time of her death.
Only partial remains of the Oviraptor have ever been discovered, so its reconstruction relies on studying a similar dinosaur: the Citipati.
The Oviraptor's entire body is covered entirely in feathers. It uses its feathery arms to insulate eggs as they incubate.
The Oviraptor's diet remains largely a mystery. Its short, toothless beak suggests it could eat anything from lizards, clams, or even seasonal fruits.

pachycephalosaurus.name: PACHYCEPHALOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Pachycephalosaurus, while a mouthful to say, means 'thick-headed lizard'?
Pachycephalosaurus has an extra thick skull to protect their brain when they ram their heads together in battle!
Jurassic World's Pachycephalosaurs are closer to the original in size, standing at 6 feet in height and weighing 990 pounds!
By butting heads, the Pachycephalosaurus frequently disable their implants, allowing them to temporarily escape their enclosure!

pachyceratops.name: PACHYCERATOPS
facts: Did you know that Pachyceratops is a misnomer? Its name means 'thick-horned face'!
Instead of two, large, and very deadly horns, the Pachyceratops has a 10 inch thick skull!
Like the Nasuceratops, the Pachyceratops has the same signature neck frill. Its back is also heavily armored with fused plate.
Male Pachyceratops establish dominance within their herd by butting heads. Extremely territorial, they're known to ram intruders!

pachygalosaurus.name: PACHYGALOSAURUS
facts: The Pachygalosaurus is a hybrid of the predatory Megalosaurus and the armored Pachyrhinosaurus!
With the defensive strength of the armored Pachyrhinosaurus and the sharp bite of the Megalosaurus, the Pachygalosaurus is built for battle!
The tail of the Pachygalosaurus is stronger those of most other carnivores. It can be used for defense, or in a stunning strike attack!
The flattened facial plates of the Pachygalosaurus are stronger than the Pachyrhinosaurus's and have more spikes for defense!

pachyrhinosaurus.name: PACHYRHINOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Pachyrhinosaurus means 'thick-nosed lizard' because of the size of its nose?
An adult Pachyrhinosaurus weighs 4 tons. That's the same as a hippopotamus, the third largest land mammal!
The diet of the Pachyrhinosaurus consists of tough, fibrous vegetation. Because of this, they have strong, specialized cheek teeth!
The Pachyrhinosaurus has a prominent pair of horns growing from their neck frill, instead of their face.

panochthus.name: PANOCHTHUS
facts: Panochthus lived in current-day South America during the Pleistocene.
Panochthus could reach up to 9 feet (3 meters) in length and weigh up to 3300 pounds (1500 kg)!
Panochthus is a glyptodont, which makes it a relative of modern-day armadillos!
The spiked tail of the Panochthus can be used for both offense and defense!

panthera.name: PANTHERA
facts: Panthera is one of four lethal Atrociraptors trained by Soyona Santos.
Atrociraptors are trained to hunt and kill based on a red laser pointer!
Atrociraptors stand roughly 6 feet, 6 inches tall and weigh 500 lbs.
Panthera is distinguishable from the other members of its pack by its red-orange coloring.

panthera_blytheae.name: PANTHERA BLYTHEAE
facts: Panthera Blytheae is the oldest known fossil of the Panthera genre, dating back to 5.9-4.1 million years ago.
The discovery of Panthera Blytheae confirms the Panthera genre appears first in Asia and then evolved and propagated into Africa as climate, fauna and flora shifted.
InGen's specimens confirm Panthera Blytheae is an agile and fast predator, hunting smaller prey, much like large cats of our modern world
Panthera Blytheae's fur is thick, long, and oily, reflecting adaptations to the climate where it thrived during the Miocenic and Pliocenic period.

parasaura.name: PARASAURA
facts: Did you know that Parasaura means 'near lizard?'
Like its progenitor, the Parasaurolophus, the Parasaura has a beak which it can use to crop vegetation.
Unlike other titanosaurs, the Parasaurua has a relatively short neck. An adult Parasaura can grow up to 32 feet in length!
Did you know that the Parasaura has a beautiful singing voice? Their cries can be heard floating across Jurassic World!

parasaurolophus.name: PARASAUROLOPHUS
facts: The Parasaurolophus roam freely on Isla Nubar and Isla Sorna, usually in the company of other herbivores.
Did you know that the Parasaurolophus can communicate by pushing air into its crest to create a deep sound?
Greek for 'near crested lizard', the Parasaurolophus gets its name from its distinct horn-like crest, which resembles Elvis's hair!
When Parasaurolophus fossils were discovered, its crest attracted wild ideas, including: a weapon, a snorkel, and even a nose!

parasaurolophus_gen_2.name: PARASAUROLOPHUS GEN 2
facts: This Gen 2 is identical to the original creature, with exception to the luminous coloration on its back.
The Parasaurolophus and Parasaurolophus Gen 2 live together in harmonious herds. This relationship is uncommon among other species.
The Parasaurolophus Gen 2’s favorite meal is freshwater crab, and they are most commonly located near freshwater springs on Isla Nublar and Isla Sorna.
The violet glow on the back of this special Gen 2 is the product of unusual marine DNA added during its creation.

pederpes_lux.name: PEDERPES LUX
facts: Pederpes is an early Carboniferous tetrapod, which lived about 350 million years ago!
Pederpes is currently the earliest known terrestrial animal, making it an ancient ancestor of humans!
Pederpes probably split its time between marine and terrestrial habitats.
Pederpes measured about 1 meter long!

pelecachtylus.name: PELECACHTYLUS
facts: The wings of this super-hybrid pterosaur may be slighter shorter than those of its forebears, but are twice as strong.
The Pelecachtylus has a larger gullet than the Pelecanipteryx, allowing it to store larger prey for longer flights... and consume them if necessary.
The crest of the Pelecachtylus is less elaborate than that of the Tupandactylus, but is more flexible and has sharper spines.
The powerful wings of the Pelecachtylus allows the creature to dive into deeper waters when hunting, or fly higher when hunted.

pelecanimimus.name: PELECANIMIMUS
facts: The bird-like Pelecanimimus got its name, 'pelican mimic,' for its long neck and throat pouch!
At about 8 feet long and weighing 50 to 100 pounds, it is the Pelecanimimus' 200+ teeth that impressed scientists!
While the Pelecanimimus has a rather toothy smile, its bird mimic relatives were primarily toothless.
Did you know that fossils of the Pelecanimimus were discovered in 1993 in Spain, in the Cuenca Province?

pelecanipteryx.name: PELECANIPTERYX
facts: Did you know that Pelecanipteryx means 'pelican wing'? This hybrid gets its distinct beak from the Pelecanimimus!
The Pelecanipteryx has a wingspan of 15 feet. A modern Great white pelican has a wingspan of 12 feet!
Pelecanipteryx has special teeth for catching and storing fish in its mouth.
The Pelecanipteryx hunts by diving into water, scooping up its prey, and then emerging in a flurry of water and wings!

phorusrhacos.name: PHORUSRHACOS
facts: Phorusrhacos gets its name from Greek. It has been translated as ‘rag thief’ and ‘branch holder.’
Did you know that at 8 feet in height, the Phorusrhacos weighs 290 pounds?
Although flightless, the Phorusrhacos is a predatory bird. Its small wings have sharp hooks, which it uses to grip its prey!
The Phorusrhacos has a curved, pointed beak, which it uses to pierce the skull of its prey!

pierce.name: PIERCE
facts: Pierce is a Kentrosaurus—armed with long shoulder and tail spikes. These aren’t just for show—when threatened, Pierce knows how to swing that tail with precision!
Though built for defense, Pierce isn’t aggressive by nature. In Camp Cretaceous, this stegosaur shows calm loyalty, proving that even the toughest dinos can have a gentle side.
Pierce’s low-slung body and plated back make him look like a living tank. This natural armor helped him stand his ground against predators and protect those around him.
Unlike many dinosaurs on Isla Nublar, Pierce develops a bond with the campers—showing trust, bravery, and a heart as strong as his spikes.

platecarpus.name: PLATECARPUS
facts: This fourteen foot monster isn't actually a fish, but an aquatic lizard! It lives in the water, but breathes air like a whale!
Platecarpus has different types of scales all over its body. Some are good for swimming, some for defense, and some for attack!
Platecarpus has a short snout, which makes it easier for the reptile to measure distance in the water and zero in on prey!
Platecarpus eats small fish instead of large prey. While hunting, this aquatic lizard uses speed instead of size!

platypterygius.name: PLATYPTERYGIUS
facts: Platypterygius is a dolphin-like ichtyosaur that roamed around the Eromanga Sea, currently inland Australia.
Platypterygius' name comes from its close-knit fin bones, which gave it a 'flat wing' to reduce water resistance.
Platypterygius was one of the first ichthyosaurs to give birth to live pups, instead of laying eggs.
Platypterygius gave birth to its young tail first, to prevent drowning during birthing.

plesiosaurus.name: PLESIOSAURUS
facts: Feeling the Plesiosaurus was closer to modern reptiles, William Conybeare and Henry De la Beche named it ‘near lizard’.
Did you know that the Plesiosaurus was the first plesiosaur to be discovered? It was unlike anything they’d seen before!
In classical art and reconstructions, the Plesiosaurus was often depicted with its neck arcing out of the water.
Many unconfirmed Plesiosaurus sightings have been reported in modern history. Most famously at Loch Ness in Scotland!

plesiosuchus.name: PLESIOSUCHUS
facts: This creature lived during the Kimmeridge stage, which is named after a village located on England's Dorset coast. Dorset is where Plesiosuchus fossils were first discovered.
Paleontologists have yet to discover a complete set of Plesiosuchus remains, making it difficult to classify this creature. However, most experts believe it is crocodilian.
Scientists estimate that the adult Plesiosuchus grew to be approximately 17 ft long. That’s 2 feet longer than the modern American Crocodile!
Plesiosuchus had large, ridged, rectangular-shaped teeth. These teeth - in combination with a powerful jaw bone - made chewing through thick material quite easy.

pliosaurus.name: PLIOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Pliosaurus means ‘more lizard’? It’s colloquially known as ‘Predator X’!
The Pliosaurus can reach up to 40 feet in length. Propped on its end, that’s nearly 4 stories high!
Unlike other plesiosaurs, the Pliosaurus has a massive head and jaws, a stocky body, and a short neck.
With 12 inch long teeth, the bite of the Pliosaurus is devastating to other marine reptiles!

plotosaurus.name: PLOTOSAURUS
facts: Of the mosasaurs, the Plotosaurus is one of the best adapted swimmers. Its name literally means ‘swimmer lizard’.
Did you know that an adult Plotosaurus can grow up to 43 feet in length?! That’s nearly as long as a school bus!
A deep diver, the Plotosaurus has a streamlined and rigid forward body that reduces drag, allowing it to swim faster.
The Plotosaurus has specially adapted scales similar to a shark. These scales create vortices which reduce drag even more!

postosuchus.name: POSTOSUCHUS
facts: Did you know that the Postosuchus gets its name from Post Quarry, Texas? Its name means 'crocodile from Post'!
Jurassic World's Postosuchus clones are quadruped amphibians. It's now believed the original Postosuchus walked on two legs!
The Postosuchus is one of the largest carnivorous reptiles from the late Triassic period. Adults can reach 13 feet in length!
Although a semi-aquatic dinosaur, the Postosuchus prefers to hunt on land, preying on anything that enters its territory.

poukadei.name: POUKADEI
facts: The Poukadei's wings also have claws, making it especially unique among Ingen's creations.
As it matures, the colors of its feathers start to resemble old depictions of giant birds in maori mythology.
Enhanced by hybrid DNA, the Poukadei is strong enough to carry a defeated prey to devour it elsewhere.
Due to its specific wingspan and size, it is a very fast and nimble predator. It is however harder for it to sustain long-term flight.

preondactylus.name: PREONDACTYLUS
facts: The Preondactylus is a pterosaur with a distinctlive long tail from the Late Triassic period.
This dinosaur is a fully developped flier, able to soar in the air with precision.
Its long tail serves to provide stability and accuracy in flight, much like the feathers on an arrow.
They mostly eat insects along their flight paths at high speeds.

prestosuchus.name: PRESTOSUCHUS
facts: Did you know that Prestosuchus means 'fast crocodile'?
An adult Prestosuchus can grow up to 17 feet in length and weigh 900 pounds. A Kodiak bear weighs 1800 pounds!
The Prestosuchus has sharp, serrated teeth perfect for cutting into the flesh of its prey!
The first Prestosuchus fossils were discovered in 1938 near the city of Sao Pedro do Sul dating back to the Late Triassic period!

prionosuchus.name: PRIONOSUCHUS
facts: Did you know that Prionosuchus means 'sierra crocodile'?
The Prionosuchus prefers a humid, tropical environment with plenty of lagoons, rivers, and streams.
Weighing up to 800 pounds, a full grown Prionosuchus can reach 30 feet in length!
The Prionosuchus is adapted to an aquatic environment. Its elongated, tapered snout and sharp teeth are suited for ambushing fish.

priotrodon.name: PRIOTRODON
facts: Did you know that Priotrodon means 'sierra-measured tooth'?
Like the Dimetrodon, the Priotrodon is a mammal-like reptile. It uses its sail to regulate its body temperature!
Did you know that the Priotrodon has teardrop-shaped teeth? They're unique to sphenacodontids.
The Priotrodon can move quickly on land or in water! Its sprawled legs are specially designed for both!

proceratosaurus.name: PROCERATOSAURUS
facts: Proceratosaurus means 'Before Ceratosaurus' or 'Before Horned Lizard' since it was once believed to be an ancestor of this predator.
At 3.5 meters (11 feet long) Proceratosaurus always has to be on the lookout for larger predators, even while hunting!
You may not be able to tell from its small size, but Proceratosaurus is actually one of the earliest known Tyrannosaurs!
The long, slender jaws of Proceratosaurus allow this dinosaur to make fast, scissor-like bites.

procoptodon.name: PROCOPTODON
facts: Procoptodon lived in Australia during the Pleistoscene, surviving until about 50,000 years ago.
One type of Procoptodon, P. goliah, stood up to 8-10 feet (2.7-3.3 meters) tall, making it the largest kangaroo to ever live!
Many scientists believe the Procoptodon is directly related to the modern day Banded hare-wallaby.
Each front paw of the Procoptodon has two extra-long fingers used to grab the foliage it eats.

prognathodon.name: PROGNATHODON
facts: Pronounced pro-nayf-o-don, the Prognathodon’s name means ‘forejaw tooth’.
In 1998 a complete skull fossil of the Prognathodon was found in The Netherlands. It was nicknamed ‘Bèr’!
At 46 feet long, the Prognathodon is a mid-sized mosasaur with bony rings surrounding its eyes.
The Prognathodon has specialized, dual-purpose teeth adapted for crushing shells and shearing flesh!

proterogyrinus.name: PROTEROGYRINUS
facts: Proterogyrinus fossils have been found in the UK, and the United States. They date to about 331-323 million years ago!
Proterogyrinus is a reptilomorph. It is likely this group is a common ancestor of many modern day reptiles!
Proterogyrinus is fully capable of walking on land, but due to its short limbs and length, it is more agile underwater.
Proterogyrinus can grow up to 2.5 meters in length. While small compared to some prehistoric creatures, it was likely a top predator of its time!

protostega.name: PROTOSTEGA
facts: The Protostega’s name means ‘first roof’ after its carapace and plastron (breastplate).
Nose to tail, the Protostega can grow up to 11 feet in length. That’s pretty big for a sea turtle!
Like the Archelon and modern leatherback turtle, the Protostega has a soft shell!
Did you know that the Protostega is the second largest sea turtle that ever lived? It’s overshadowed by the Archelon!

psephoderma.name: PSEPHODERMA
facts: Did you know that Psephoderma means ‘pebbly skin’? It gets its name from the pebbly surface of its shell!
Feeding primarily on shellfish, the Psephoderma has a beak-shaped mouth, allowing it to pick its prey from between rocks.
Resembling a turtle with a long tail, the Psephoderma has a segmented shell like a horseshoe crab.
The Psephoderma is quite small compared to other placodonts, growing up to only 5 1/2 feet in length!

pteranodon.name: PTERANODON
facts: Did you know that the Pteranodon is best known as a 'Pterodactyl'?
There were three variations of the Pteranodon created by InGen. The version created for Jurassic World is closer to the original.
The Pteranodon recreated for Jurassic World is closer to the original animal, with a wingspan of 26-33 feet!
Did you know that Pteranodon means 'toothless wing'? Its name is a misnomer, as the Pteranodon actually has teeth!

pteranodon_gen_2.name: PTERANODON GEN 2
facts: Pteranodon Gen 2 parents force their young out of the nest earlier than most other pterosaurs.
With a wingspan of 23-30 feet, Pteranodon Gen 2 is slightly smaller than the original.
Pteranodon Gen 2 is a master of agility, and can fly as fast as 100 miles per hour!
Allegedly, InGen added altered reptilian DNA to Pteranodon Gen 2 in order to create its striped coloration.

pteraquetzal.name: PTERAQUETZAL
facts: Pteraquetzals do not produce bristle feathers until their first moult.
With a wingspan of 30 feet, there's no question this hybrid inherited its remarkable size from the Quetzalcoatlus!
Pteraquetzals live in small flocks of up to 5. Flocks will break up if too many new members join for reasons that remain unclear.
The massive crest on the mature Pteraquetzals represents flock seniority. Opposing flocks will attack the Pteraquetzal with the largest crest as a signal of disrespect.

pterodactylus.name: PTERODACTYLUS
facts: Did you know that Pterodactylus was first named in 1809 by French anatomist George Cuvier? Its name means 'winged finger'.
Originally believed to be a sea creature, the Pterodactylus is the first pterosaur to be named and identified as a flying reptile!
The Pterodactylus has around 90 conical teeth, reducing in size from the tip of its jaw to the back!
The original Pterodactylus was quite small, with a wingspan of 3 feet. A Canadian goose has a wingspan between 4 and 6 feet!

pterodaustro.name: PTERODAUSTRO
facts: The Pterodaustro lived 105 million years ago in what is now South America! Fossils were first discovered in Argentina.
Did you know that Pterodaustro comes from 'pteron de austro'? It means 'wing from the south' in Greek.
Like a flamingo, the Pterodaustro wades through shallow water to catch its meal!
Did you know that the Pterodaustro has a thousand teeth? These bristle-like strain algae and small creatures from the water!

purussaurus.name: PURUSSAURUS
facts: Remains of the Purussaurus have been discovered all across South America.
This creature is theorized to be the largest of all the known crocodyliformes!
Due to its bulk and size, the Purussaurus needs to ingest massive quantities of food!
Much like other types of crocodiles, the Purussaurus is able to perform the infamous "Death Roll" to battle other creatures.

pyroraptor.name: PYRORAPTOR
facts: Biosyn engineers creatures from around the world - like the Pyroraptor, a Cretaceous Period dinosaur discovered in Southern France.
While not the largest raptor, the Pyroraptor has scythe-like claws on its back feet measuring up to 2.5 inches in length!
Its name, Pyroraptor, means 'fire thief.' It has nothing to do with the dinosaur, but the forest fire that led to its discovery.
Did you know that the Pyroraptor weighed 400 pounds? That's the same as an adult Black Bear!

pyroraptor_dominion.name: PYRORAPTOR DOMINION
facts: This agile creature made its nest around the frozen lake of the dam above Biosyn Sanctuary where it hunted many preys!
The Pyroraptor is an excellent hunter and is a strong swimmer! This suggests that this dinosaur is also a dangerous foe in the water.
For a time, it was thought the Pyroraptor was a dromaeosaurid, but recent research suggests it's actually an unenlagiid! This means it's a member of a different group of theropods.
The Pyroraptor is notable for its feathers. Its fossils show evidence of quill knobs, which suggests it had a full coat of feathers, just like many birds do today.

quetzalcoatlus.name: QUETZALCOATLUS
facts: Biosyn engineered the Quetzalcoatlus from fossils first discovered in the state of Texas in 1971.
Did you know that this airplane-sized pterosaur is one of the largest flying animals of all time?!
With a wingspan of around 40 feet, the Quetzalcoatlus is the size of a MIG-29 fighter jet!
This featherless behemoth gets its name from Quetzalcoatl, a Mesoamerican flying serpent god!

quetzalcoatlus_gen_2.name: QUETZALCOATLUS GEN 2
facts: This Late Cretaceous period pterosaur is one of the largest animals to ever fly.
The Quetzalcoatlus GEN 2 spreads its wings a whopping 36 feet!
Named after the Aztec feathered serpent god, Quetzalcoatlus commands the skies over Jurassic World!
By catching the right air currents, this toothless pterosaur is capable of flying across continents, or even around the world!

quetzaljara.name: QUETZALJARA
facts: Quetzaljara is the result of fusing Pteraquetzal—itself a hybrid of Quetzalcoatlus and Pteranodon Gen 2—with Tapejara DNA, creating a tri-lineage super hybrid built for the skies.
With the sleek agility of Tapejara and the wingspan of Quetzalcoatlus, Quetzaljara soars with unmatched precision—twisting, diving, and striking with midair mastery.
Quetzaljara’s vibrant head crest isn’t just for show—it reflects its Tapejara roots and is believed to be used for communication, intimidation, and balance during flight.
This pterosaur doesn’t just dominate the skies with power—it uses advanced instincts and hybrid intelligence to outmaneuver foes and control the aerial battlefield.

rajasaurus.name: RAJASAURUS
facts: The Rajasaurus gets its name from a combination of Sanskrit and Greek, meaning 'king of lizards'.
The Rajasaurus was a rare fossil find. It was first discovered in the Narmada River Valley in Gujarat, India in 2003.
Did you know that during the Late Cretaceous Period, India was a part of a giant continent called Gondwana?!
Preserved Rajasaurus skulls show a distinctive small horn above the eyes, unique to this king of lizards!

rajastega.name: RAJASTEGA
facts: Did you know that Rajastega means 'king's roof'? Its name is derived from Sanskrit.
Unlike the Rajasaurus, the Rajastega only weighs 1200 pounds. That's as much as an American Quarter horse!
The Rajastega has a pronounced, almost horn-like crest on its head. This crest can reach up to 2 feet in length!
Although a terrestrial predator, the Rajastega has a primitive set of gills, despite being unable to swim.

rebel.name: REBEL
facts: This spinoceratops is the brother of another named Angel.
Despite its name, this dinosaur has a much tamer behavior compared to its sister.
DNA analysis from Rebel confirms that the Spinoceratops inherits more behavioral traits from the Sinoceratops.
Playful behavior observed from Angel and Rebel confirm it is the main way these dinosaurs learn through their continued growth.

red.name: RED
facts: Named for her unique coppery-red scales, Red is one of four lethal Atrociraptors engineered for viciousness.
Like her Atrociraptor sisters, Red was trained to hunt down anyone marked with a red laser pointer.
Red is famous for hunting Barry before being trapped by Owen in her crate!
Red's coppery color may come from copperhead snake DNA.

rexy.name: REXY
facts: Rexy is the ultimate Apex predator! Never one to back down from a fight, Rexy will take on any challenger that comes her way.
At 8.4 tonnes, Rexy is a massive beast. This is the equivalent of 18,518 pounds, roughly the same weight as a school bus!
Rexy's massive jaw can open 80 degrees, giving her a bite you don't want to mess with. She's taken down many rivals with those teeth!
After escaping the Lockwood Estate along with many other dinosaurs, Rexy now lives in the protected environment at Biosyn Valley.

rhamphorhynchus.name: RHAMPHORHYNCHUS
facts: Did you know that Rhamphorhynchus means 'beak snout'? Its name comes from the shape of, you guessed it, its beak!
The Rhamphorhynchus has a sharp beak and needle-like teeth, ideal for snapping up fish and small cephalopods!
Rhamphorhynchus fossils were believed to belong to an ancient bird. It wasn't until 1831 that it was recognized to be a pterosaur!
The Rhamphorhynchus has a wingspan of 6 feet. That's the same as a Great blue heron!

rhinoprotodon.name: RHINOPROTODON
facts: This wooly mammal might look cuddly from a distance, but the effect dissipates as you get close enough to realize its massive size.
Thriving on an entirely vegetarian diet, this mammal is actually quite gentle once you get to a point of trust with it.
Rhinoprotodon has cubic scat, like the wombat!
Rhinoprotodon's pouch is backward facing to avoid filling with dirt while digging its extensive warrens.

rhizodus.name: RHIZODUS
facts: Did you know Rhizodus is the largest known freshwater fish? It measures close to a whopping 23 feet!
Rhizodus is a survivor. It dominated large rivers and swamps throughout the entire Carboniferious period. That's over 60 million years!
Many fish related to Rhizodus swallow their prey whole. Rhizodus however uses its 8 inch fangs to viciously tear prey apart before eating it!
The discovery of a near complete Rhizodus fossil was published in 1880. It was found below sea level and under a foot of shale!

rhomaleosaurus.name: RHOMALEOSAURUS
facts: At 23 feet, the Rhomaleosaurus was one of the biggest plesiosaurs of its time!
The first Rhomaleosaurus found by humans was discovered in 1848 in Yorkshire, England.
With some almost complete specimens, the massive Rhomaleosaurus is among the best preserved marine reptiles!
As an apex predator, Rhomaleosaurus ate a wide range of sea creatures including ichthyosaurs, molluscs, and even other plesiosaurs!

rinchenia.name: RINCHENIA
facts: Rinchenia lived in Cretaceous epoch, around 70 million years ago, in what is now Mongolia.
The type specimen of Rinchenia is a nearly complete fossil discovered in 1984.
Rinchenia is named after Byambyn Rinchen, the great Mongolian linguist!
Rinchenia's estimated mass is roughly 25kg (55lb) and it measures 1.7m (5.6 ft) in length.

rinchicyon.name: RINCHICYON
facts: This newest InGen creation adds considerable muscle and bulk from the Amphicyon to the nimble and agile Rinchenia!
This hybrid's most notable traits include its thick forelimbs and developed back muscles.
These adaptations alter its hunting strategies, making it a wrestler able to pin down prey once it catches up or ambushes them.
Due to its small teeth compared to its size, it prefers to hunt for smaller prey which it can dominate through strength.

rodrigues_solitaire.name: RODRIGUES SOLITAIRE
facts: Rodrigues solitaire is a close relative of the famous Dodo!
Whereas the Dodo was native to the island of Mauritius, Rodrigues solitaire hails from the island of Rodrigues, east of Madagascar.
Like the Dodo, Rodrigues solitaire is flightless, and went extinct due to overhunting by European colonizers.
Rodrigues solitaire probably went extinct between 1730 and 1760.

sah_panthera.name: SAH PANTHERA
facts: This hybrid's dentition is able to crush bones, which is part of its regular diet.
Sah Panthera diverges from Panthera Blytheae by enhancing the frame of the Sarkastodon, making it one of the sturdiest and thickest felines among the cenozoic hybrids.
This hybrid's body trades some amount of speed for considerable endurance and stamina, making it able to hunt much larger prey than other creatures in the Panthera family.
InGen's scientists noticed that the Sah Panthera's senses are keener than expected, combining sensitive whiskers, eyes adapted to nightvision, and heightened sense of smell.

salamander_16.name: SALAMANDER 16
facts: Genetically modified from the Microposaurus, Salamander 16 is one of the most intimidating amphibians in Jurassic World.
Salamander 16's wide stance and strong neck help it pull taller opponents down to its level.
The spikes along Salamander 16's jaw prevent its latest meal from breaking free of its powerful bite.
The ridges on Salamander 16's back are extremely sharp but surprisingly flexible, allowing them to slip between the cracks of an opponent's armor.

sarcomantarx.name: SARCOMANTARX
facts: This newly developed hybrid evolved with a distinct pigmentation, which was not planned by InGen scientists.
Behavioral studies seem to indicate it prefers rocky environments and mountains rather than what was expected based on its parent DNAs.
Scientists theorize the spikes on its back inherited from the Animantarx serve as camouflage among the craggy areas, blending its shape in the environment.
Its hunting patterns indicate inclination towards ambush, usually hunting smaller prey with sudden snaps of its powerful jaw.

sarcosaurus.name: SARCOSAURUS
facts: The Sarcosaurus is one of the earliest known theropods from the Jurassic Period.
Due to its place in the evolution chain, fossils were often misidentified due to discrepancies in scale with other dinosaurs of that period.
Scientists theorize that the Sarcosaurus served as a gatekeeper in the early Jurassic period by serving as predator to all the smaller dinosaurs.
DNA reconstruction at InGen confirms that the Sarcosaurus is a branching point in dinosaur evolution, where it splits into much larger and smaller evolutions in different families.

sarcosuchus.name: SARCOSUCHUS
facts: Sarcosuchus means 'flesh crocodile', but National Geographic called the dinosaur 'SuperCroc' in a television special. The nickname has stuck ever since!
Did you know, at 40 feet in length, that the Sarcosuchus is the largest crocodile-like reptile to ever live?!
This Cretaceous Period leviathan weighs around eight tons. An elephant weighs 6.5 tons at best!
The immensely strong jaws of the Sarcosuchus allow it to easily take down even the largest predatory dinosaurs.

sarkastodon.name: SARKASTODON
facts: The Sarkastodon, meaning 'flesh-tearing tooth', is named after its bear-like maw.
The Sarkastodon has strong canine teeth which it uses to seize its prey. Its sharp premolars easily slice through flesh!
At 3 feet in height, an adult Sarkastodon can reach 10 feet in length! That’s the average length of an Indochinese tiger!
A powerful predator of its time, the Sarkastodon is a hypercarnivore, meaning that its diet is exclusively made up of meat.

scaphognathus.name: SCAPHOGNATHUS
facts: Fossils of the Scaphognathus were first described in 1831 by August Goldfuss, who misidentified it as a new Pterodactylus species.
Did you know that Scaphognathus means 'tub jaw'? It comes from the blunt, boat-shape of its lower jaw.
Unlike other pterosaurs, the Scaphognathus is not nocturnal, preferring to hunt and socialize during the day!
The wingspan of the Scaphognathus is only 3 feet wide! That's the same as a Glossy ibis!

scelidosaurus.name: SCELIDOSAURUS
facts: The small Scelidosaurus measures only 4 meters in length when mature!
With shortened forelimbs, Scelidosaurus can move in a combination of bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion.
This low-to-the-ground herbivore feeds mostly on ground ferns.
Scelidosaurus lived on the Jurassic supercontinent of Laurasia, and was discovered in modern-day Dorset, England.

scolosaurus.name: SCOLOSAURUS
facts: The first fossils of Scolosaurus found were near-complete specimens!
The unearthed fossils of Scolosaurus also had traces of skin, making its reconstruction easier.
Scolosaurus has considerably durable skin and scales, making it very resilient to predators.
The tail club of the Scolosaurus has a distinct round shape, contrary to other species which have it either longer or wider.

scorpios_rex.name: SCORPIOS REX
facts: Researchers hoped to control the combination of Albertosaurus and Deinonychus traits in this hybrid, but nature found a way to surprise them.
This creature has longer arms than a typical Tyrannosauroid, allowing it to more easily trip and rend its prey.
The bony extrusions of the Deinonychus' tail are evenly distributed as defensive ridges and spikes along the spine of this hybrid creature.
The barbed crimson spikes adorning this hybrid's tail are flexible like quills, suggesting a frightening new kind of ranged attack.

scorpios_rex_gen_2.name: SCORPIOS REX GEN 2
facts: The Scorpios rex is an experimental precursor to the Indominus rex. Little is known about the genetic history of this vicious GEN 2 variant.
The Scorpios rex GEN 2 is known for its extreme aggression and instability, making this creature difficult to contain.
Like the Scorpios rex, this GEN 2 variant possesses venomous quills that it can shoot from its body. These quills can paralyze its prey, adding to its already formidable predatory abilities.
Unlike other hybrids, Scorpios rex variants possess gaunt and twisted features which may reflect their unstable genetic makeup.

secodontognathus.name: SECODONTOGNATHUS
facts: The most striking thing about this flying dinosaur is the forehead crest that merges with its back sail.
The Secodontognathus' back sail helps it maintain equilibrium while flying.
The jaws of the Secodontognathus are lined with sharp teeth designed for rending the medium-sized vertebrates that make up its food.
The Secodontognathus' name means 'Cutting Tooth Jaw', which reflects its terrible bite.

secodontosaurus.name: SECODONTOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Secodontosaurus comes from Latin and Greek for 'cutting-tooth lizard'?
Due to its long jaws, paleontologist Robert Bakker dubbed the Secodontosaurus a 'fox-faced finback'.
The Secodontosaurus has slender jaws and consistent sized teeth specialized for catching fish and burrowing prey!
Growing up to 9 feet in length, an adult Secodontosaurus can weigh over 250 pounds!

segnosaurus.name: SEGNOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Segnosaurus means 'slow lizard'? It comes from the size of this stocky herbivore!
Weighing in at 4 tons, the Segnosaurus can reach lengths of 26 feet!
The Segnosaurus is an omnivore. Its unique teeth are perfect for cutting, chewing, and tearing into its food!
The Segnosaurus is one of the few clones in Jurassic World to have feathers. They range from flat, neutral tones to brilliant plumage!

segnosuchus.name: SEGNOSUCHUS
facts: Segnosuchus is a hybrid of the herbivore Segnosaurus and the amphibian Postosuchus.
Segnosuchus does not have the feathers of its hybrid parent Segnosaurus. This is due to its amphibious DNA components.
Many scientists agree Segnosuchus looks quite a bit like the fictional Titanosaurus from the Godzilla franchise. The similarity is a coincidence of genetics.
A fully evolved Segnosuchus exhibits a unique blue color. This helps it camouflage in water.

seymouria.name: SEYMOURIA
facts: Seymouria is a type of Seymouriamorph, a small but widespread terrestrial and semi-aquatic tetrapods.
Seymouria is technically an amphibian, but is well adapted to life on land!
Like modern frogs, Seymouria may have a larval tadpole stage!
Today, Seymouria is considered an important creature in the transition from ancient to modern reptiles!

shunosaurus.name: SHUNOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that the Shunosaurus was discovered in Sichuan Province in China? Its name means 'Shu lizard'.
The Shunosaurus is one of the smaller sauropods, with a characteristically short neck. An adult can grow up to 31 feet in length!
To defend against threats, the Shunosaurus has a clubbed tail equipped with 2 inch long spikes which it can swing like a flail.
With its extremely narrow and pointed skull, the Shunosaurus' upper and lower jaws function like garden shears.

sinoceratops.name: SINOCERATOPS
facts: Sinoceratops are herbivores, but their young are omnivorous and will eat anything during a growth spurt.
Sinoceratops live in herds, which are typically led by the oldest female.
The average adult Sinoceratops will grow to 20 feet in length.
To date, the only known Sinoceratops fossil is a partially intact skull.

sinosauropteryx.name: SINOSAUROPTERYX
facts: Sinosauropteryx means 'Chinese reptilian wing!'
Sinosauropteryx was the first dinosaur not immediately related to birds to be discovered with evidence of feathers!
Sinosauropteryx lived in what is now Northeastern China in the Cretaceous period.
Sinosauropteryx was quite small, measuring up to 1 metre but weighing only 1.2 pounds!

skoolasaurus.name: SKOOLASAURUS
facts: The Skoolasaurus retains traits of cold-blooded lizards much like the Koolasuchus.
Its teeth are wide and serrated, useful for catching prey and crushing them.
The head of the Skoolasaurus is very heavy since it inherits considerable bone density and mouth width from its hybrid components.
The Skoolasaurus is much more adept at navigating on land than the Koolasuchus since it benefits from thicker skin, protecting it from predators.

skoonasaurus.name: SKOONASAURUS
facts: This Superhybrid combines Sonorasaurus DNA and the Skoolasaurus for a heavily armored brachiosaurid.
The Skoonasaurus retains the wide mouth of the Skoolasaurus but adapts its teeth to a herbivore lifestyle in order to eat large chunks of foliage in a single bite.
Due to amphibian DNA in this dinosaur's lineage, it seems to favor a diet of trees able to grow in wetlands.
The feet of the Skoonasaurus are wider than other brachiosaurids to account for better maneuvrability in rivers and swamps.

smilodon.name: SMILODON
facts: Famously known as the ‘Sabre Toothed Tiger’ or ‘Sabre Toothed Cat’, the Smilodon is an iconic Ice Age predator!
The Smilodon, meaning 'knife tooth', has slender, 11-inch teeth which are serrated on the front and back sides.
The Smilodon can reach up to half a metric ton in mass, whereas its smaller cousin, S. Gracilis, is the size of a modern leopard!
Described as 'he who brings devastation' by Danish naturalist Wilhelm Lund, the Smilodon earned its name in 1842.

smithetoceras.name: SMITHETOCERAS
facts: Smithetoceras' powerful form gives it more speed and strength than a modern bull!
Smithetoceras is an apex predator equipped to hunt its hybrid ancestor Synthetoceras!
The horns of Smithetoceras are used for mating displays, and have little use as defensive weapons.
Smithetoceras lives in small packs or prides. Like silverback gorillas, the coloring of an alpha Smithetoceras will differentiate it from its peers!

smoothie.name: SMOOTHIE
facts: Don’t let Smoothie’s size fool you! Even as a hatchling, this baby Ankylosaurus has a tough hide and a curious spirit—ready to explore the world with a wag of its tail.
Named Smoothie by the Chaos Theory team, this little dino charmed everyone with its round shape, calm demeanor, and love of belly rubs.
Smoothie may not have its full armor or clubbed tail yet, but those signature Ankylosaurus traits are just beneath the surface, waiting to grow with every bite and step.
With every wobble and snort, Smoothie proves that courage isn’t about size—this dino’s loyalty and bravery shine even in the smallest moments.

sonorasaurus.name: SONORASAURUS
facts: The Sonorasaurus was found in the Sonoran desert, from which its name is derived, in 1994.
Sonorasaurus is the oldest known brachiasaurid from the Middle Cretaceous period.
The existence of the Sonorasaurus destroys the theory that sauropods/titanosaurs died out in North America by the Cretaceous period.
An original contender for the Sonorasaurus' name was 'Chihuahuasaurus' but it was decided it would be a silly name for a 49 foot long dinosaur.

sphenacodon.name: SPHENACODON
facts: Sphenacodon means "wedge point tooth". This carnivore’s mouth contains a variety of razor-sharp teeth, which make tearing meat effortless.
Sphenacodon is a close relative of Dimetrodon, as can be seen from its large and narrow skull. Also, both creatures have long torsos, short limbs, and move as quadrupeds.
Some scientists believe that Sphenacodon had exceptionally strong back muscles which strengthened the creature’s mobility, and even made it capable of leaping.
Sharp bones jutting from the vertebrae make up this creature’s back crest. There are at least two known species of Sphenacodon, and each is distinguished by their different crest lengths.

spinoceratops.name: SPINOCERATOPS
facts: The Spinoceratops, also sometimes referred to as the Sinospino, is a hybrid dinosaur, created with the DNA of a Sinoceratops and the DNA of a Spinosaurus GEN 2.
The Spinoceratops is a generally peaceful hybrid. It's been observed that male Spinoceratops are more peaceful than females, though this may simply be personality differences.
Spinoceratops dinosaurs are omnivores. They tend to feed mostly on plants, but also occasionally eat fish as well.
The Spinoceratops mostly resemble the Sinoceratops. However, they have inherited the distinctive sail of the Spinosaurus, giving them a unique look.

spinoraptor.name: SPINORAPTOR
facts: Did you know that Spinoraptor means 'spined thief'?
The Spinoraptor is a hybrid dinosaur cloned from Spinosaurus and Utahraptor DNA!
While much smaller than its giant progenitor, the Spinosaurus, the Spinoraptor is still formidable at 15 feet tall.
With a 4 foot tall sail, what strikes fear into the Spinoraptor's enemies are her 8 inch claws designed for disembowelment.

spinosaurus.name: SPINOSAURUS
facts: One of the largest carnivores, the Spinosaurus outweighs the T. rex by a ton. InGen's clone reached nearly 20 feet in height!
Did you know that Spinosaurus clones have two head crests, opposed to the single head crest of the original dinosaur?
The skull of the Spinosaurus measures at 6 feet in length, large enough to snap up a person without issue.
The sail of InGen's Spinosaurus is also underdeveloped. The original dinosaur had a sail that was 6 feet high!

spinosaurus_gen_2.name: SPINOSAURUS GEN 2
facts: Some scientists speculate that Spinosaurus had a hump for storing water instead of a sail. InGen rejected this theory when they designed both the original and Gen 2.
Spinosaurus and Spinosaurus Gen 2 both have nostrils that are located near the eye, just like a crocodile!
Both Spinosaurs have a longer length and heavier weight than the T. rex, making them the biggest carnivorous dinosaurs in Jurassic World.
The first Spinosaurus fossils to be discovered were destroyed during WWII when the Munich museum was bombed. It took another 50 years before more Spinosaurus remains were excavated.

spinosaurus_rebirth.name: SPINOSAURUS REBIRTH
facts: This Spinosaurus confirms the long-debated speculations that the specie is semiaquatic !
The leg bones of the Spinosaurus have osteoscleroris, helping it swim by floating.
The dorsal sail of the Spinosaurus helps it swim, as well as intimidate or attract others of its kind.
The Spinosaurus is an adept hunter, able to use a wide variety of tactics and strategies depending on its chosen prey.

spinotasuchus.name: SPINOTASUCHUS
facts: This superhybrid was created to test for aquatic adaptations left dormant in the raptor bloodline.
Agile in water, Spinotasuchus can often be found hunting plesiosaurs near the shoreline!
At night, Spinotasuchus uses the cover of water to sneak up on prey dwelling on the shore.
