The green coloration of the Spinotasuchus helps it camouflage with algae, like a modern crocodile.

spinotops.name: SPINOTOPS
facts: Spinotops is a rare example of a super hybrid, formed by merging the DNA of Spinoceratops—itself a hybrid of Spinosaurus Gen 2 and Sinoceratops—with the spiked defenses of Kentrosaurus.
Thanks to its ceratopsian ancestry and stegosaurian infusion, Spinotops boasts both a powerful frill and tail spikes—offering offense and defense in one fearsome package.
The genetic memory of Spinosaurus Gen 2 provides raw power, while Sinoceratops contributes agility and flair. Kentrosaurus completes the trio with razor-sharp reflexes and a tail built for battle.
Spinotops isn’t just strong—it’s smart. Its hybrid lineage grants it adaptive instincts, blending herding defense tactics from ceratopsians with the strategic tail strikes of stegosaurs.

stegoceratops.name: STEGOCERATOPS
facts: With a hefty spiked tail and two 3 foot long horns, the Stegoceratops is equipped with the ultimate defense against apex predators!
Combining the DNA of a Stegasaurus and Triceratops, its name means 'roof-horned face'.
The Stegoceratops large, spiked frill and thick back spikes easily thwart the awesome chomp of a hungry Tyrannosaur or Allosaurus!
What sets this majestic beast apart is its size, weighing in at 15 tons. That's the same as an F-18 fighter jet!

stegosaurus.name: STEGOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that the average Stegosaurus has a brain the size of a walnut?
Due to its small brain, 19th century scientists thought the Stegosaurus had a second brain in its hip. In other words, its butt!
To up the wow factor when InGen successfully cloned the Stegosaurus, their clones are 40 feet long, instead of 32.
The new clones created by Masrani Global Corporation appear to be genetically identical to the original Stegosaurus.

stegosaurus_gen_2.name: STEGOSAURUS GEN 2
facts: Stegosaurus fossils have been found throughout the US, Europe, and in Asia!
Stegosaurus' spinal plates could serve for defense, display, or heat regulation!
As Stegosaurus GEN 2 evolves, its hide takes on a rich, coppery color!
When the first Stegosaurus fossils were discovered, some paleontologists believed its plates lay flat on its back!

stegouros.name: STEGOUROS
facts: Stegouros is an ankylosaur from the Cretaceous period.
Stegouros is a new discovery, found in 2018 in Chile!
Stegouros means 'roof tail,' named for the unique shape of its tail end.
Stegouros is the only ankylosaur so-far discovered with its unique tail end shape!

struthiomimus.name: STRUTHIOMIMUS
facts: The Struthiomimus is a genus of ornithomimidae, a family of dinosaurs noted for their resemblance to ostriches.
Struthiomimus' have keratinous toothless beaks, which may have been used for a variation of feeding strategies.
Compared to other ornithomimidae, Struthiomimus' hands are proportionately longer in relation to the rest of their arm.
Struthiomimus' are roughly 8 feet long with strong hind limbs adapted for fast movement.

stygimoloch.name: STYGIMOLOCH
facts: Stygimoloch communicates primarily through snorts and grunts, like today's antelope.
Most of Stygimoloch's aggressive interactions are with each other.
Stygimoloch has a beak as well as teeth, allowing it to effectively nip bite-sized parts of the plants it eats.
The spikes at the back of this dinosaur change as they grow, being more prominent in younger Stygimoloch and shorter in the adults.

styracosaurus_lux.name: STYRACOSAURUS LUX
facts: Styracosaurus lux exhibits bioluminscence, a natural glow-in-the-dark!
The bioluminescence of the Styracosaurus lux is caused by bony tubercles of the skull that shine through the skin!
It is believed that, like some modern chameleons, this light effect is used for communication in the darkness among members of its species.
More research on the social behavior of the Styracosaurus lux is needed to learn more about the full power of its glow!

styxosaurus.name: STYXOSAURUS
facts: The Styxosaurus is named after the River Styx that, in Greek mythology, separated the land of the living from that of the dead.
At 40 feet long, the Styxosaurus has a incredibly long neck that makes up half of its body’s length!
Like other plesiosaurs, the Styxosaurus relies on small stones called gastroliths to digest its food.
Did you know the Styxosaurus swallows its prey whole? It has interlocking, conical sharp teeth that puncture and grip prey!

suchodus.name: SUCHODUS
facts: Suchodus is closely related to another extinct crocodyliform, the Metriorhynchus.
Two different species of Suchodus existed during the Middle and Late Jurassic period.
Suchodus measures about 13 feet (4 meters) long, but scientists believe the creature could potentially grow up to 15 feet (4.6 meters)!
Suchodus fossils have only been found in England and France. Other Metriorhynchid fossils have been found across Europe, North and South America.

suchomimus.name: SUCHOMIMUS
facts: Greek for 'crocodile mimic', the Suchomimus is 35 feet long and weighs 5 tons. That's more than a basking shark!
Recreated by InGen, the clones of the Suchomimus are dark blue with yellow and have proto feathers on the back of their arms!
Did you know that the Suchomimus has backward pointed teeth? It's adapted for holding prey instead of slicing or tearing.
Despite it being nearly as large as a T. rex, the Suchomimus prefers a diet of fish over hunting land dwellers!

suchoripterus.name: SUCHORIPTERUS
facts: Did you know that Suchoripterus means 'crocodile wing'? It gets its name from the shape of its snout, which resembles a crocodile!
With a wingspan of 10.5 feet, the Suchoripterus is slightly larger than a Griffon vulture!
The Suchoripterus is an excellent swimmer and it's not uncommon to see flocks of Suchoripterus bathing in shallow water.
Unlike the Dsungaripterus, the Suchoripterus lacks a tweezers-like beak. Instead of prying open shellfish, it crushes it.

supersaurus.name: SUPERSAURUS
facts: In Wyoming, USA, there is a skeleton of the Supersaurus nicknamed 'Jimbo'!
Although not unlike the Diplodocus in design, what sets the Supersaurus apart is its sheer size at 110 feet long!
Did you know that Supersaurus means 'super lizard'?
Discovered in 1972 in Colorado, the Supersaurus lived in the Late Jurassic Period, more than 145 million years ago!

suprannotitan.name: SUPRANNOTITAN
facts: Did you know that Suprannotitan means 'super tyrant titan'? What a title!
Weighing a staggering 15 tons, the Suprannotitan is one of the largest carcharodontosaurids (shark-toothed lizards)!
An adult Suprannotitan can reach up to 50 feet in length and 20 feet in height!
The Suprannotitan is much stockier than its Tyrannotitan progenitor. Its powerful legs allow it run up to 40 mph!

synthetoceras.name: SYNTHETOCERAS
facts: Synthetoceras is a large hoofed mammal with three horns. It has two on the top of its head, and one large forked horn coming from its nose!
At 750 pounds, Synthetoceras is similar in size and shape to a modern moose!
Only the male Synthetoceras has the species' trademark third horn, which is used in competitions for territory!
Synthetoceras is a protoceratid, an extinct group of hoofed mammals. At six feet long, it's the biggest of its family!

tanycolagreus.name: TANYCOLAGREUS
facts: Did you know that Tanycolagreus means 'long-limbed hunter'?
An adult Tanycolagreus can exceed lengths of 13 feet and weigh 265 pounds!
The Tanycolagreus has a blunt snout. Its head is large, elongated, and rectangular because of this.
Clones of the Tanycolagreus at Jurassic World have exhibited primitive social skills similar to the Velociraptor!

tapejalocephalus.name: TAPEJALOCEPHALUS
facts: The dense membranes in this pterosaur's bones allow it to support itself in flight.
Like the Euoplocephalus, the armor of the Tapejalocephalus is made of bony scutes.
The skin of this superhybrid's wings is thicker than any other pterosaur, allowing it to lift its heavy body into the air.
Due to its weight and invulnerability from above, the Tapejalocephalus flies much lower than some other pterosaurs.

tapejalosaurus.name: TAPEJALOSAURUS
facts: The Tapejalosaurus is a hybrid of the fruit eating pterosaur, Tapejara, and the carnivorous Monolophosaurus!
The two strong legs of the Tapejalosaurus make it one of the best dinosaurs at snatching prey from the air!
Although it has sharp teeth, the Tapejalosaurus is actually an omnivore, eating both fruit and meat!
As Tapejalosaurus grow, so do their impressive fringes. They use them mostly to intimidate each other!

tapejara.name: TAPEJARA
facts: The Tapejara was best suited for the seashores of South America, where it lived over 100 million years ago!
Like the Tapejara, the language its name originates from is also extinct. It comes from a Tupi word for 'old being'.
What is perhaps most distinct about the Tapejara is its large head crest, which can grow up to 3 feet in length!
Did you know that the Tapejara is 12 feet long? That's longer than the biggest boa constrictors!

tarbosaurus.name: TARBOSAURUS
facts: Tarbosaurus hatchlings are playful, but as they mature their behavior becomes highly aggressive.
Tarbosaurus is an apex predator, and a close relative of Tyrannosaurus rex. Its name means "Alarming Lizard".
This carnivore’s front teeth are extremely sharp and closely packed together, allowing it to bite through tough skin.
By clapping its powerful jaws together, the Tarbosaurus signals that it has made a kill. This sound acts as a warning to other creatures.

temnodontosaurus.name: TEMNODONTOSAURUS
facts: Temnodontosaurus is one of the oldest and largest ichthyosaurs known to science.
Temnodontosaurus means 'cutting-toothed lizard', named for its rows of jagged teeth.
Temnodontosauruses ate ammonites, cephalopods, and sometimes even their own young.
Temnodontosaurus teeth had deep, strong roots to prevent loss or breakage while cracking ammonite shells.

thalassodromeus.name: THALASSODROMEUS
facts: Thalassodromeus has a highly ornate head crest resembling a pharoah's crown.
It was originally thought that Thalassodromeus would skim feed, like a pelican, but we now know that to be false.
Thalassodromeus likely hunted on the ground, like the modern stork.
T. Sethi is named after the egyptian god Set, due to the namer confusing a picture of Amun (who wears the pharoah's headdress) for Set.

the_big_one.name: THE BIG ONE
facts: Nicknamed by Robert Muldoon, The Big One is the Alpha female Velociraptor of Jurassic Park.
This creature is also known as 'Clever Girl' for her capacity to lethally outsmart her human prey!
The Big One rules over two Velociraptor subordinates.
Using a bait and ambush maneuver, The Big One is the predator of both Robert Muldoon and Ray Arnold!

ceratosaurus_gen_2.name: THE CERATO JP3
facts: The cranial structure of The Cerato is slightly different from the original. It features a more prominent eyebrow crest, shielding its eyes from the sun.

In the wilds of Isla Sorna, Ceratosaurus could be recognized by its prominent nasal horn and bold coloration. However, while it can be every bit as dangerous as other carnivores, it still bowed out when it sniffed Spinosaurus’s Territory.
Silent in the jungle mist, Ceratosaurus ambushed prey with its dark hide. Yet in a realm of deadlier giants, Scorpios rex soon outmatched it.
The nasal horn of The Cerato seems to serve as a mark of status and might among others of its species.

the_spino.name: THE SPINO
facts: The Spino is most famous for its epic battle with the Tyrannosaurus rex, establishing itself as a new apex predator.
Measuring approximately 43 feet in length, the Spinosaurus was one of the largest known carnivorous dinosaurs, surpassing even the Tyrannosaurus rex in sheer size.
With adaptations for both land and water, the Spinosaurus was a skilled hunter in aquatic environments, pursuing its prey across both land and water.
The Spinosaurus is easily identified by the large sail on its back, composed of elongated spines. This structure may have played a role in thermoregulation or display behaviors.

therizinosaurus.name: THERIZINOSAURUS
facts: The 8-foot long arms of the Therizinosaurus are a subject of great interest to Biosyn's engineers- especially since those arms are tipped with 3-foot long claws!
Did you know the Therizinosaurus has imposing arms? At 8 feet long, they are tipped with 3 foot claws the length of human arms!
Standing at nearly 33 feet tall, the Therizinosaurus is taller than an adult giraffe!
Weighing in at 5 tons, the Therizinosaurus weighs more than a white rhino!

therizinosaurus_gen_2.name: THERIZINOSAURUS GEN 2
facts: Like other Therizinosauridae, the Therizinosaurus Gen 2 are herbivores, enjoying a healthy diet of foliage and vegetation.
Scientists increased the Gen 2 incubation period, resulting in a more ferocious dinosaur! Therizinosaurus Gen 2 is fiercer than their original counterpart.
The Therizinosaurus and the Therizinosaurus Gen 2 are both characterized by their exceptionally large claws. Frightening!

The Therizinosaurus Gen 2 uses its long arms to reach food in the trees. It's been noted that Therizinosaurus Gen 2 seems to be less picky than the Therizinosaurus when it comes to its choice of vegetation to snack on.

thylacosmilus.name: THYLACOSMILUS
facts: Often called a Saber Toothed Tiger and grouped with the Smilodon, this predator is actually evolutionarily closer to marsupials than cats!
Thylacosmilus grew to about the size of a modern jaguar, making it one of the largest metatherian predators.
The Thylacosmilus has a very weak bite and as a result, hunts by first immobilizing prey with its paws, then slicing with its saber teeth.
Like the teeth of some modern rodents, the long fangs of the Thylacosmilus continue to grow over its entire life!

tiger.name: TIGER
facts: This dinosaur has been named that way because of its distinctive orange hue and black stripes.
Tiger hunts using hit-and-run tactics, surprising its prey and then retreating until the next assault.
Tiger, like other Atrociraptors, is a social animal and prefers to be in a pack.
Tiger's teeth and claws are specialized for hunting larger prey than itself.

titanoboa.name: TITANOBOA
facts: Titanoboa simply means 'Titanic Boa'. As the largest snake ever discovered, these creatures can grow up to 42 feet!
The Earth was much warmer 60 million years ago, which allowed cold blooded creatures like this snake to grow to such a large size!
The Titanoboa is so large that it can swallow a crocodile whole!
Although it was the largest predator of its time and had no competition from dinosaurs, the Titanoboa ate mostly fish and avoided land prey.

titanoboa_gen_2.name: TITANOBOA GEN 2
facts: Despite being separated by several million years, the Titanoboa is very closely related to current snakes in the Pacific Islands.
The Titanoboa is considered a Superpredator, meaning it was at the top of the food chain during its time period, having no predator of its own.
Contrary to popular belief, its body is not round. The vertebrae are shaped with a large base and are at their highest in the middle.
During design of the Titanoboa Gen 2, InGen scientists discovered it had more teeth than previously thought, distinctly more than our modern day snakes.

toro.name: TORO
facts: Though Toro was cloned for exhibition in Jurassic World, he ultimately proved to be too aggressive for the park and was moved to an enclosure away from the public.
Similar to the rest of his species, Toro is a reddish-brown color with black patterns along his body. He also has a scar across his snout, giving him a particularly scary look.
Just like other Carnotaurus, Toro weighs 4,800 pounds. This is approximately the same size as a fully grown rhinoceros!
The name Carnotaurus means "meat-eating bull", an apt description for an aggressive dinosaur like Toro. This is also how he got his name: Toro means "bull" in Spanish!

triceratops.name: TRICERATOPS
facts: Greek for 'three-horned face,' the Triceratops is easily identified by its distinct three horns and large frill.
Combining the backwards facing frill with the length of its skull, the Triceratops' has a head length of over 7 feet!
InGen's original Triceratops clones were shades of brown and beige. They lived in their own paddock with an alpha named 'Lady Margaret'.
Did you know that the Triceratops can run at speeds of up to 10 mph? A crocodile moves at 11 mph!

triceratops_gen_2.name: TRICERATOPS GEN 2
facts: Scientists mistakenly identified the first Triceratops fossils as horns from a giant bison.
Like the original Triceratops, the Gen 2 has a habit of accidentally eating West Indian lilac berries, which are known to make them ill.
Adult Triceratops Gen 2 can weigh up to 22,000 lbs. That's about the same weight as the original.
This ceratopsian's horns jut horizontally from the skull, making them a dangerous weapon in battle.

trinacromerum.name: TRINACROMERUM
facts: Named after its powerful flippers, Trinacromerum means ‘three-tipped femur.’
Feeding on small fish, the Trinacromerum has thin, needle-like teeth and elongated jaws.
The Trinacromerum is a powerful swimmer, relying on its long flippers to propel it through water!
Did you know that Richard Ellis referred to the Trinacromerum as a four-flippered penguin?

troodon.name: TROODON
facts: Did you know that the Troodon is often labelled as the 'smartest dinosaur' on account of its unusually large brain?
While its brain was proportionally large compared to its 75 pound body, the Troodon has the intelligence of an average chicken!
Had it not gone extinct, it's speculated that the Troodon might have evolved to a human level of intelligence.
The name Troodon comes from Greek for 'wounding tooth' due to its serrated teeth.

tropeognathus.name: TROPEOGNATHUS
facts: Did you know that Tropeognathus means 'keel jaw' in Greek? The tip of its nose is not unlike the fins under a ship.
The beak of the Tropeognathus set this pterosaur apart, as it has a large fin-like crest on its nose and chin.
The Tropeognathus has a wingspan of 20-25 feet. That's the length of a modern crocodile
The shape of its beak aids the Tropeognathus in hunting its primary food source, fish!

tropeogopterus.name: TROPEOGOPTERUS
facts: Did you know that the Tropeogopterus has a wingspan of 18 feet? It's one of the lightest and fastest pterosaurs!
The Tropeogopterus' name means 'keel wing,' highlighting its incredible agility!
The Tropeogopterus has a combined keel-like crest on its beak and pointed head.
Because of its long legs and light build, the Tropeogopterus has no trouble launching itself into the air!

tsintaosaurus.name: TSINTAOSAURUS
facts: Tsintaosaurus had a unicorn-like crest on its head that might have been part of its mating display.
This lake-dwelling hadrosaur had a large tail, and paddle-like arms to help it swim.
Resonators in the Tsintaosaurus' crest produced distinctive mating calls.
Tsintaosaurus could stand on its hind feet to reach vegetation on various levels.

tuojiangosaurus.name: TUOJIANGOSAURUS
facts: Similar to the Stegosaurus in build, the Tuojiangosaurus's back plates were much more triangular and pointed.
Discovered in 1973, the Tuojiangosaurus fossils reveal that it was the earliest example of a stegosaur known to humanity!
Did you know that the Tuojiangosaurus was discovered in Sichuan Province of China?
Its name, Tuojiangosaurus, is a combination of Chinese and Greek meaning 'Tuo River lizard'.

tupandactylus.name: TUPANDACTYLUS
facts: Tupandactylus was originally classified as being part of the Tapejara species. Later studies revealed enough differences to create its own category.
Tupandactylus' wingspan can reach up to 5 meters. That's almost double the wingspan of the Albatross, which has the largest wingspan of any living bird.
Tupandactylus fossils have only been discovered in Brazil.
Although its diet remains open for debate, Tupandactylus is generally considered to be a piscivore.

tupuxuara.name: TUPUXUARA
facts: Tupuxuara is named after a spirit in Tupi mythology.
Tupuxuara's wingspan can reach up to 5 meters (15 feet) or more!
Paleontologists believe the crest of the Tupuxuara grew as the creature aged, like a lion's mane.
Tupuxuara is a member of the Thalassodromidae family, which flourished in Brazil during the early Cretaceous.

tusoteuthis.name: TUSOTEUTHIS
facts: Tusoteuthis can grow up to 20-35 feet (6-11 meters)!
Though some call it a giant squid, Tusoteuthis is actually more closely related to the Vampire Squid than the modern-day Giant Squid.
Fossil evidence from the stomach of a Cimolichthys suggests Tusoteuthis was hunted by other large predators.
Although the Tusoteuthis was prey for some large predators, it’s likely it was also a mosasaur hunter!

tylosaurus.name: TYLOSAURUS
facts: The Tylosaurus, meaning 'knob lizard', is named for its elongated, cylindrical snout, which it uses to ram prey.
Viewed from the side, Tylosaurus was a big animal. But viewed from the front, it would have presented a very small cross-section.
With over eighty vertebrae in its tail, the Tylosaurus, like other mosasaurs, relies on its tail for locomotion!
An apex predator, the Tylosaurus has been known to feed on other mosasaurs and sharks to maintain its ecosystem!

tyrannolophosaur.name: TYRANNOLOPHOSAUR
facts: A hybrid of the Tyrannosaurus rex Gen 2 and the Dilophosaurus Gen 2, the Tyrannolophosaurus inherited the hunting skills of both predecessors, making it a fearsome beast.
Like the Tyrannosaurus rex Gen 2, the Tyrannolophosaurus is sensitive to any changes in their surroundings.
The Tyrannolophosaurus is shorter than a T-Rex, but no less powerful. Their exceptionally strong teeth and jaws allow them to tear through meat and sinew with ease.
What it lacks in height, the Tyrannolophosaurus makes up for in sound - their call is particularly low and menacing, scaring off potential threats in the area.

tyrannosaurus_rex.name: TYRANNOSAURUS REX
facts: Did you know that Tyrannosaurus rex translates to 'tyrant lizard king' in Ancient Greek and Latin?
At the hips, the Tyrannosaurus rex was 13 feet tall. That's the same height as a full grown female giraffe!
The Tyrannosaurus rex has 58 teeth. The average shark has roughly 50!
Did you know that the first Tyrannosaurus rex cloned by InGen was nicknamed 'Rexy'?

tyrannosaurus_rex_gen_2.name: TYRANNOSAURUS REX GEN 2
facts: Tyrannosaurus rex Gen 2's instinctive attraction to scent and movement makes her virtually unable to ignore changes in her surroundings - even on a full stomach.
The Tyrannosaurus rex Gen 2 is a master at inertial feeding, and is able to throw a hundred pound chunk of meat up to 40 meters in the air.
The Tyrannosaurus rex Gen 2 prefers hunting in rocky desert terrains.
A Tyrannosaurus rex Gen 2 has never been observed to have a broken tooth - this is thanks to their abnormally dense enamel.

tyrannotitan.name: TYRANNOTITAN
facts: Its name meaning 'tyrant titan', the Tyrannotitan can reach an impressive 15 feet tall!
The Tyrannotitan can weigh between 4-7 tonnes. That's more than an African elephant!
Did you know that the Tyrannotitan has chisel-like teeth?
The InGen variety of the Tyrannotitan is mottled with varying shades of grey and deep blue.

uintatherium.name: UINTATHERIUM
facts: The Uintatherium, which is slightly larger than a modern rhino, also has long fang-like teeth and claws!
Because of their size and armor, the Uintatherium is nearly immune to predation. It's just too big for anything to take down!
While the Uintatherium's fangs can be used in battle, they primarily help it strip vegetation from the bottom of rivers and pools!
Uintatherium is big, but has a very small brain. With no predators and abundant food, there's no reason to be smart!

umoonasaurus.name: UMOONASAURUS
facts: ‘Umoona’ is an aboriginal word that means ‘long life,’ so this plesiosaur's name translates to "long life lizard.'
The Umoonasaurus was discovered in Coober Pedy, which is considered the ‘opal capital of the world’!
Unlike other plesiosaurs, the Umoonasaurus has three distinct crest-ridges on its skull.
Did you know that fossils of the Umoonasaurus were found preserved in opal?

unayrhynchus.name: UNAYRHYNCHUS
facts: Did you know that Unayrhynchus means 'black water snout'? It gets its name from the colour of its beak!
The Unayrhynchus is quite light, weighing only 100 pounds. That's about as much Doberman pinscher!
The average Unayrhynchus stands at 2 feet in height and can run up to 60 mph!
Although its diet consists of vegetation, the Unayrhynchus is an omnivore. Its needle-like teeth are perfect for catching fish!

unaysaurus.name: UNAYSAURUS
facts: The Unaysaurus lived 200-225 million years ago during the late Triassic Period on the then super continent of Pangaea.
Did you know that the Unaysaurus is related to the famous and much larger Plateosaurus?
This small dinosaur stands at barely 3 feet tall and weighs no more than 200 pounds!
Derived from the Tupi word 'unay,' the Unaysaurus' name translates to 'black water lizard'!

urtinotherium.name: URTINOTHERIUM
facts: Urtinotherium means 'Urtyn beast.' It is named for the Urtyn Obo region in Mongolia.
Urtinotherium is a member of the family Indricotherinae. This is a group of long-limbed, hornless rhinoceroses of the Eocene epoch.
Urtinotherium fossils are found mostly in eastern and central Asia.
While large, Urtinotherium is dwarfed by its relative the Paraceratherium, which could grow 4.8 metres (15 feet) tall or more!

utahraptor.name: UTAHRAPTOR
facts: Did you know that the Utahraptor is the largest raptor to ever live? At 1100 pounds, it weighs the same as a polar bear!
Like other raptors, the Utahraptor has large, curved claws on its second toes. These claws can reach a terrifying 10 inches!
The Utahraptor lived approximately 50 million years before the better known Velociraptor!
The Utahraptor was named by paleontologist James Kirkland. He is currently working on excavating an entire pack of the predatory theropod!

valkyrie_77.name: VALKYRIE 77
facts: This fearsome genetically modified Pteranodon claims the skies over Jurassic World as its own.
The reinforced beak allows Valkyrie 77 to pierce even the toughest armor, while its sharp teeth allow each strike to inflict maximum damage.
The prominent bony crest on Valkyrie 77 lends extra force to its power-dive attacks
Valkyrie 77's sharp-edged wings lets it cut through aerial opposition with ease.

velociraptor.name: VELOCIRAPTOR
facts: Meaning 'swift seizer', the Velociraptor is a well-known dinosaur. In fact, they're often referred to simply as 'raptors'.
InGen's Velociraptor clones differ vastly from the originals. They are much larger and featherless.
Did you know that the extinct Velociraptor would have only weighed 30 pounds and stood at 3 feet tall?!
At six feet tall, InGen's creations are highly intelligent and deadly, with 6 inch retractable claws!

velociraptor_gen_2.name: VELOCIRAPTOR GEN 2
facts: One Velociraptor Gen 2 was found living among a pack of Velociraptor, proving that both types can live together harmoniously.
The Velociraptor Gen 2 is known to ‘tease’ other creatures, sometimes without any intent to harm.
The Velociraptor Gen 2 runs with longer strides than the first Velociraptor.
The yellow spines on the matured Velociraptor Gen 2 signify to her pack that she is qualified to lead.

woolly_mammoth.name: WOOLLY MAMMOTH
facts: Scientists can tell the age of a Woolly Mammoth by counting the amount of rings in its tusks - just like a tree!
Ancient humans hunted Woolly Mammoths, probably to extinction. These hunts are shown in prehistoric cave paintings: the oldest art ever!
Over 35 Woolly Mammoths have been discovered throughout the years. Some are almost complete and frozen solid!
Although most Woolly Mammoths went extinct 10,000 years ago, a small population survived in the arctic until 1650 BCE!

woolly_rhinoceros.name: WOOLLY RHINOCEROS
facts: This creature’s name references the main difference between it and the modern day Rhinoceros: a thick, woolly fur coat.
The Woolly Rhinoceros stores fat in the hump on its back, just like the modern day camel!
This herbivore's mouth has sharp incisors in the front and flat molars in the back.
The Woolly Rhinoceros is thought to have evolved from Dicerorhinus, a huge two horned mammal that survived during the Pleistocene Epoch.

wuerhosaurus.name: WUERHOSAURUS
facts: Did you know that Wuerosaurus means 'Wuerho's reptile'? Its name is derived from the city of Wuerho in China.
Reaching a length of 23 feet, an adult Wuerhosaurus weighs 4 tons! That's as much as a rhinoceros!
What distinguishes the Wuerhosaurus from its more famous cousin, the Stegosaurus, are its small rounded, rectangle-shaped plates.
Like the Stegosaurus, the Wuerhosaurus has four bony spikes on its tail, which it uses to defend itself and its young.

xinathodon.name: XINATHODON
facts: This powerful aquatic hybrid spends most of its time hunting near the surface of the water.
Xinathodon is a surface creature. However, as it ages, it becomes more comfortable in deeper waters.
Xinathodon develops purple coloring as it matures. This helps it camouflage at the surface of reflective waters.
Xinathodon's facial spikes are defensive, but also help it sense tremors in the water that may be caused by prey!

xiphactinus.name: XIPHACTINUS
facts: Did you know that Xiphactinus means ‘sword-ray’?
The Xiphactinus is similar in build to the tarpon. Both have streamlined bodies and upturned mouths.
Fully grown, the Xiphactinus can reach between 15-20 feet in length.
With its enlarged teeth, the Xiphactinus can grip larger prey, consuming it a bite at a time!

yudon.name: YUDON
facts: The Yudon is a hybrid of the Troodon and the land carnivore Yutyrannis!
Though not the largest hybrid in Jurassic World, the impressive feathered spines of the Yudon make it one of the most intimidating!
The Yudon is smaller but faster than the Yutyrannus, and with more strength pound for pound!
The oversized head and powerful neck muscles of the Yudon allow it to take down prey larger than itself!

yutyrannus.name: YUTYRANNUS
facts: Meaning 'feathered tyrant', the 'yu' in Yutyrannus comes from Mandarin Chinese.
InGen's Yutyrannus is one of the only cloned species to maintain its feathery down.
Did you know that the Yutyrannus lived during the early Cretaceous period in what is now northeastern China?
A relative of the T. rex, the Yutyrannus is known as both the largest feathered dinosaur and theropod!

yuxisaurus.name: YUXISAURUS
facts: Yuxisaurus means 'Yuxi lizard,' so named for its discovery in the Yuxi area of China!
Very recently discovered, the first scientific papers on Yuxisaurus were published in 2022!
Yuxisaurus is an armoured ornithiscian similar in build to a Nodosaurus.
The impressive dermal plates of Yuxisaurus cover much of its body and help to protect it form predators.

zalmonodon.name: ZALMONODON
facts: Zalmonodon hatchlings can take up to 6 months before learning to fly. This delay is likely the result of its mammal DNA.
Zalmonodon’s preferred meal is berries, and is an expert at plucking them off bushes while in mid-flight.
Zalmonodons nest on cliffs, where they store food. They stockpile berries in their nests to eat during the dry season.
This hybrid’s wingspan can reach up to 35 feet, making it even bigger than the pterosaur it was fused from!

zalmoxes.name: ZALMOXES
facts: Named for an ancient European deity, Zalmoxis, this dinosaur was discovered in Romania in 1899!
Zalmoxes has a pointed skull and narrow beak. It feeds mainly on low-lying vegetation and berries.
At 10 feet long, the Zalmoxes weighs about 500 pounds. That's the same weight as a large male black bear!
Did you know that because of its rotund build, the robust Zalmoxes is one of the smaller genus' of bipedal herbivores?

zhejiangopterus.name: ZHEJIANGOPTERUS
facts: The Zhejiangopterus gets its name from the Zhejiang Province, where its fossils were found in 1986.
Unlike other pterosaurs of the Late Cretaceous period, the Zhejiangopterus lacks a large, bony crest on its head!
The Zhejiangopterus' wingspan ranges from 11 and 15 feet in width. The American bald eagle's wingspan is only 7.5 feet!
Did you know that the Zhejiangopterus only weighs between 50 and 70 pounds? That's the same as a golden retriever!
